item.title: The NFL should relocate the Steelers-Saints game in Paris to London
item.description: NFL scraps multiple Saturday events due to ongoing protests.
item.content:encoded:
With one day more to go until the Steelers and Saints play in Paris, the NFL shouldn't wait one hour more to relocate the game.

No matter how safe and secure Stade de France will be for the game, it's not safe for NFL fans to be in Paris due to protests that from time to time morph into full-blown riots.

Consider the latest moves made by the league as to the collateral activities. Via the Associated Press, the NFL announced on Saturday the closure of its "NFL House" event, due to "potential accessibility issues." Previously, the Steelers Fan House event was scrapped. The "Saints House" has been postponed until Sunday.

Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department issued a security alert cautioning "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" to "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings."

Why would the NFL insist on pressing forward? The risk, however big or small it may be, isn't worth it.

The league has said security at the game will be enhanced. Which necessarily means security resources that could be utilized elsewhere in the city are being devoted to something that is far from a necessity.

Also, no matter how secure the stadium is, the fans who have bought tickets to the game will need to get to the perimeter where the NFL's security plan activates.

A soccer match between PSG and Lyon recently was moved from Sunday to Monday, at the direction of French authorities. If the NFL won't do the prudent thing and move the game to London, the powers-that-be in Paris should direct the NFL to bump Steelers-Saints to Monday, too. (That would shift the game broadcast to Monday morning or afternoon, New York time. Which could inadvertently unlock a new standalone window for future NFL games.)

It's surprising that it's gotten to this point. The warning signs have been obvious for weeks. On Friday, even the President chimed in. And the league's determination (or, more accurately, stubbornness) to proceed has led to a situation in which the NFL may still be forced to make an eleventh-hour-and-fifty-seventh-minute decision to do something other than play the game as scheduled. Which, for the teams, will only add to the overall in-season inconvenience of traveling to another country to play a football game.

There's no reason to wait. They should make the move now.

We're not privy to all of the specifics. The generalities continue to suggest that the league absolutely should pivot from the plan to play in Paris at 3:30 p.m. local time on Sunday.

Why assume the risk that any fan will be endangered as they try to get to the game? Why take any risks that the enhanced security will be overrun by an event that the protester-rioters could see as a perfect opportunity to make their message resonate internationally?

It seems to be increasingly obvious that relocation of the game is the right call. Even if nothing happens, there's already a cloud over the league's first-ever Paris game. And if there's even one incident in connection with playing the game as planned, the NFL will risk being dubbed what the French call les incompétents.

item.title: To survive Detroit shootout, Packers should look to Thanksgiving win
item.description: The Packers are likely to face a high-scoring matchup on Sunday. Here are three ways they can survive.
item.content:encoded:
It’s no secret the Packers game against the Detroit Lions on Sunday is likely to be a shootout.

As a byproduct of their stellar offense and inability to slow anyone on defense, Detroit hasn’t played a low-scoring game all year. In every Lions game so far this season, both teams have scored at least 21 points. In four of the five, both teams have scored at least 24. In two, both teams scored at least 30. If you like offense, you’ll probably like watching the Detroit Lions play football.

The Packers, meanwhile, haven’t really been in a high scoring game this year. The Packers have only broken 30 once, and both times their opponents have done it, the Packers haven’t seemed super interested in keeping pace. Obviously they’ll have to avoid that outcome if they want a chance against the Lions.

Fortunately, there’s a recent example of how the Packers should approach a game likely to result in a high-scoring shootout: their Thanksgiving day showdown with the Lions last year. That game alone should have showed the Packers exactly the kind of aggressive, playmaker-focused game they’ll need to play to beat the Lions this week.

It starts with fourth down conversions. Matt LaFleur has trended back towards aggressiveness on fourth downs this year, and his choices against the Lions last November shows how that approach can pay off.

The Packers converted all three fourth down tries last year, scoring two touchdowns (a 27-yard strike to Dontayvion Wicks and a one-yard score by Romeo Doubs) and putting the game away on their final drive.

The third conversion deserves special attention. Facing a 4th and 3 on the Lions’ 45-yard line with just under two minutes to go, the Packers made the high-risk, high-reward decision to go for it. Given that the Lions had no timeouts, a conversion would end the game. But throw incomplete or come up short, and the Lions would have been in business, needing less than 20 yards to get into field goal range.

Matt LaFleur put the ball in Jordan Love’s hands, and Love delivered, finding Wicks for a 16-yard completion.

That sort of approach should again pay dividends against the Lions, who you can expect to be aggressive whenever they have the ball as well.

The Packers’ aggressiveness should also extend to their playcalling. Last year, LaFleur and Love went deep often. Seven of Love’s 30 passing attempts that day were to targets more than 20 yards downfield. He completed four of those seven targets for 126 yards and two touchdowns. That’s not quite as good as Love’s heat check performance against the Bears, but it’s close enough,and considering how poor the Lions’ passing defense is by virtually every measure (in or near the bottom quarter in almost every stat you can find), I think we can reasonably assume he’ll have a chance to move the ball against the Lions this week. 

They should take advantage.

They’ll need some defensive plays, though. Last year, Micah Parsons brought plenty. He came up with three sacks, two of which were on third down. On a second half third down, the Lions were lined up on the Packers’ four-yard line, trailing by 10. Parsons broke through and took down Jared Goff for a nine-yard loss, and the Lions kicked a field goal. If not for the sack, would Detroit have attempted a field goal or gone for it all? We’ll never know, but Parsons’ sack definitely changed the calculus.

Parsons obviously won’t be on the field this week, but the need for playmaking is no less important, especially with Zaire Franklin on the sideline. Defensive stops may not forestall a shootout entirely, but a few crucial big plays could tilt the field.

Looking to the past is no guarantee of success. The Packers have certainly changed quite a bit since last Thanksgiving. But the lessons learned in that widely watched game are still relevant today, and if the Packers can run the same script, they’ll be in great shape.

item.title: Breaking down the numbers: Cowboys at Eagles preview
item.description: Who do you think is going to win on Monday night?
item.content:encoded:
Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lincoln Financial on Monday Night Football to take on the Philadelphia Eagles.

Cowboys key stats from last week

Dak Prescott threw for 258 yards on an astonishing 54 attempts. He’d finish the game with a 65.2 passer rating.

Javonte Williams rushed the ball just 11 times against Green Bay for 41 yards.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 15 receptions on 29 targets, racking up 143 receiving yards

Brevyn Spann-Ford split time with Jake Ferguson at a near 50/50 rate. The second-year tight end continues to improve his stock this season.

The defense didn’t force a third-down stop until the near the six-minute mark in the second quarter. They tightened up in the second half, allowing just two third-down conversions and a total of 83 yards.

Eagles key stats from last week

The Eagles offense gained a total of 222 yards last week in their loss against the Panthers. Just 35 of those yards came on the ground from the beat up Philadelphia rushing attack.

Tanner McKee threw the ball 45 times, finishing with a 77.5 passer rating.

The leading receivers for the Eagles were DeVonta Smith (seven receptions, 75 yards) and Dallas Goedert (six receptions, 61 yards).

Stay grounded

This game could come down to which team’s rushing attack is the most successful.

Last week, Javonte Williams and the run game had a few moments, but Dallas got away from it far too early. Coach Brian Schottenheimer has been under scrutiny this week for completely abandoning the run game, a tendency we’ve seen often throughout his career in Dallas. This week, it’ll be imperative to run a balanced offense against an Eagles defense that has struggled, but isn’t void of talent.

On the Eagles side, it looks like Saquon Barkley has a good shot at returning to the lineup this week. This offense will not want Tanner McKee to throw the ball over 40 times again if it can be avoided. The Eagles offensive line has struggled to get much going for any of their running backs this season. But Dallas has also had their share of problems in limiting opponent’s rushing attacks. The formula is clear for Philadelphia, but can they execute?

What do the numbers mean?

This week, we’ve got two underperforming NFC East teams in a primetime Monday night matchup. The Eagles offense has struggled this season, even before the unfortunate Jalen Hurts health situation. The Cowboys have been mostly healthy on offense, but have lacked the killer instinct situationally while also no-showing the last two weeks. So which team has a better shot at putting up points and securing the win?

As bad as Dallas has been the last two weeks, this offense still features two of the league’s scariest targets on the outside. They still have a top 10 quarterback who, at times, elevates himself into top five territory. The offensive line still features several All-Pro and Pro Bowl players. Make no mistake, they are dangerous and can go off any given week.

This week, if coach Schottenheimer can return to a balanced offensive attack, the Cowboys will take home the win. The Eagles simply do not have the firepower to keep up, even against a struggling Dallas defense. And if Prescott and the offense can jump out to an early lead, this could get ugly for Philadelphia.

The Cowboys have not put a holistically decent product on the field, especially the last two weeks. They have certainly been bad. But the Eagles have been just as bad, if not worse, and are now without their franchise quarterback.

Tanner McKee is a stationary target without a good offensive line. They lack adequate talent at wide receiver, outside of DeVonta Smith. If the Cowboys defense ever had a moment to show up and get right, this would be a great time. If the Cowboys can stifle the biggest threat on the field in Barkely, this should be a long day for the Eagles backup quarterback.

Everything points to Dallas winning, which of course should scare the pants off Cowboys fans. We saw a similar situation against a backup quarterback in Tampa Bay in week five. But records aside, that Buccaneers team is better than Philadelphia. They possess more offensive weapons, they have a mobile quarterback, and Todd Bowles put together a defensive gameplan that exposed a fatal weakness. The Eagles defensive scheme is vastly different and won’t crowd the line of scrimmage throughout the game. This plays to the Cowboys favor.

Dallas has done very little to earn or trust this season. But if they can head up to Lincoln Financial and simply do their jobs against a beat up and beaten down Eagles team, this game should finish with a convincing Cowboys win.

item.title: Nate Landman out for Rams vs. Raiders
item.description: Nate Landman is out and some other NFL news on a Saturday
item.content:encoded:
Nate Landman went on the injury report this week and now he’s officially out. It’s another blow to the Rams who seem to have their 2026 season falling apart. As the injuries and losses mount up, how can this team stay positive?

A win on Sunday would go a long way, but with all the injuries, a win may be a long shot. Puka Nacua’s status is up in the air.

It was no sure thing that the Rams would play the playoffs this year, but it seems very likely, and now? It seems like a stretch as L.A. seems more likely to fall to 2-5 than 3-4.

Injury Report, Week 7 at Raiders: Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out (therams)

“Nacua left Thursday’s practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua “took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out.” McVay also said that “I don’t think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred.”

However, McVay did characterize the injury as “minor.”

“You look at it, and there’s just a little minor thing in there, and felt it where he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion, and just kind of noticed it,” McVay said. “But I don’t think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.”

Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week.

Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is “making good progress,” McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad.“

The Rams continue to receive public backing because bettors cannot believe the team is this bad. However, approximately 75% of the money is on the Raiders, with no significant action of note. The line moved from 5.5 to four.

“(Raiders head coach Klint) Kubiak’s done a great job. They’re really well coached in all three phases. They’ve been productive in all three phases. They made some big free agent signings on the defensive side of the ball. They got a bunch of different playmakers,” McVay said.“

item.title: Giving Browns DT Mike Hall Jr. even more retroactive respect for Week 4’s sack
item.description: Cleveland Browns DT Mike Hall Jr. will miss his 3rd straight game with an injury, putting his Week 4 return into context
item.content:encoded:
As the Cleveland Browns get ready to travel to Nashville to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, the top of the AFC North continues to belong to the orange and brown. Injuries, including DT Mike Hall Jr. being out this week, continue to be a big variable for the Browns and their opponents.

All the positivity heading into Week 7 wasn’t as strong if we look back to when Hall, along with DT Mason Graham, were injured in Week 4 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football.

Graham is expected to return in Week 7 after getting injured early in Week 4 and being ruled out after halftime. Just before the intermission, Hall injured his ankle, was helped off the field, and then carted into the locker room. Cleveland (and Pittsburgh) fans know what happened next for the former Ohio State defensive lineman:

Hall later said he knew his teammates needed him with Graham out for the game.

From being carted off the field to exploding for a huge third-down sack that pushed the Steelers out of field goal range, Hall’s impact was appreciated after a game where the score (27-24) might have been decided, partially, by his return and big sack.

Since that game, Hall is set to miss his third straight contest. While that may be frustrating to some Browns fans, it also puts his Week 4 return into context. Running off of adrenaline and knowing what his teammates needed, Hall not only returned to the field but made a huge impact, while dealing with an ankle injury that will have needed a month off, at least, between games played.

Three weeks later, it is clear that Hall’s ankle injury was and is significant. That adds even more respect to his Week 4 return and play.

item.title: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell on potential Tokyo game: 'It's coming at some point in the near future'
item.description: The NFL previously hosted 14 preseason games in Japan from 1976 to 2005.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has its eyes on returning to Japan with a game potentially happening in 2027 or 2028, according to commissioner Roger Goodell.

Appearing on the “NFL Daily” podcast this week, Goodell said the league’s goal is to hold a regular-season game in Tokyo at some point over the next two seasons.

"Listen, Tokyo is clearly on our list, whether it's next year or the year after," Goodell said. "It's coming at some point in the near future."

It’s not a matter of if, but when at this point. Goodell’s comments come nearly two months after NFL executive vice president of club business and international and league events Peter O’Reilly said the league had been researching returning to Japan for a game and three months since Goodell named the country as one that was being targeted as a host city.

A regular-season NFL game has never been played in Japan, but the league did host 14 preseason games there between 1976 to 2005 — 13 in Tokyo and one in Osaka.

The success of the San Francisco 49ers-Los Angeles Rams Week 1 game in Melbourne, Australia has played a role in helping the NFL learn how to pull off such a game.

"On a Friday morning at 10:30, to have 100,000 people in the stadium, it was just an incredible feeling for us. I think it's opened up new opportunities for us," Goodell said. "The travel is something we think we can manage and do it without impacting negatively on the teams. So each of these we learned something from and we benefit and we also open those other doors."

Should the NFL go to Japan, the Los Angeles Rams would likely be one of the teams involved. Under the league's Global Markets Program, the team has marketing rights in the country.

The NFL would like to increase the number of international games per season to 16 in the future. For now, owners approved a proposal to play up to 10 outside of the U.S. in 2027. Currently, there are five international games scheduled next season with Berlin, Mexico City and London (three games) set to host.

The New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers will play the sixth international game on the 2026 schedule this Sunday from Stade de France in Paris. Three more international games will be left to be played this season in Madrid, Munich and Mexico City.

item.title: Lions vs. Packers 5 Qs preview: Unpacking Jordan Love’s volatile numbers
item.description: Here’s our preview with Acme Packing Company about this Week 7 matchup between the Detroit Lions and Green Bay Packers.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh off their early-season bye, the Detroit Lions pick up where they left off against their first NFC North opponent: the Green Bay Packers.

We had the pleasure of connecting with Justis Mosqueda, the Team Community Producer for Acme Packing Company, to give us some insight into this Packers team ahead of this week’s matchup. We learned about Jordan Love’s wild mix of quick releases and deep shots amidst Green Bay’s pass-protection woes, the ongoing O-line carousel and Josh Jacobs’ potential impact on the run game, as well as Jonathan Gannon’s hyper-aggressive blitz scheme—plus much more.

1. Jordan Love’s numbers are the most fascinating thing to unpack with this Packers offense. He has the shortest time to throw in the NFL among 37 qualifying quarterbacks (2.48 seconds), yet he sports the sixth-highest average depth of target (9.5 yards) and according to Pro Football Focus, leads the league in big-time throws (15) and passing attempts of 20+ yards downfield (33).

Through six weeks of the season, what’s the story of Love between these numbers?

In short: Heroics. The offensive line performed poorly in the pass-protection game outside of Weeks 4 and 5. He has absolutely no running game to speak of. Love is taking a massive pounding week to week. It really is just the Kobe stan in Love coming out and willing the team to victory. The team also leads the NFL in drops over this time period, too, and a lot of those are on what would have been explosives and/or touchdowns. It’s incredibly frustrating to watch Love play at such a high level with the rest of the offense playing poorly around him.

2. Likely associated with Love’s performance this season is the offensive line and the running game. Injuries have thrown Green Bay’s offensive line into the centrifuge. Since the start of the season, they’ve acquired some familiar faces in Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler, and they’ve done their fair share of shuffling to figure out the best combination. Is this the week Zeitler makes his season debut? What’s your level of confidence in this line solidifying itself by the time these two teams meet again in January? 

Meanwhile, the Packers have one of the worst rushing attacks in the league–but Josh Jacobs did come off the Commissioner’s Exempt List on Monday. How much do you anticipate Jacobs playing in this game based on Matt LaFleur’s comments this week, and do you think he’s the kind of difference maker who can single handedly get this run game out of the basement?

I really think it could be. The running game has been bad all year, but at least Week 4 and 5 were games where the offensive line could at least protect Love. Last week, the Packers went into five-man protections for most of the game for the first time all season. This ended up exposing both guards a little more than anyone seemed to expect (Jacob Monk and Donovan Jennings started the year at guard before the team transitioned to Travis Glover and Laken Tomlinson). As of Thursday’s practice, the Packers were repping seven players to get ready for this game: the starting center (Sean Rhyan), the two tackles (Anthony Belton and Jordan Morgan) and four guard options (Glover, Tomlinson, Aaron Banks and Kevin Zeitler). I would not be shocked at all if we get Banks at left guard and Zeitler at right guard this week. If the Packers want to make that change before Week 9, they kind of have to do it now, because they have a short week against the Carolina Panthers after this.

I 100 percent think Jacobs is going to play this week. LaFleur has really backed him at every opportunity to do so. The team has very much been in the business of getting Jacobs back on the field, even prior to the legal process playing out. They said he’s been working out with the team and in meetings the entire time. He just hasn’t been able to practice with them. They have three open roster spots on the 53-man roster that they’re keeping open right now, and two of those (Jacobs and PUP player Jordan Riley) are probably already filled in their minds. I think Jacobs can help turn some of those -2 runs into +2 runs, but I don’t think he’s just going to come into the lineup and fix all of Green Bay’s running game issues himself.

3. Former defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley left for a head coaching gig with the Miami Dolphins, and the Packers brought in Jonathan Gannon to replace him. What are some of the most notable differences you’ve noticed between the two coordinators, have said differences been mostly positive, negative or somewhere in between, and do you feel like the eventual return of Micah Parsons will end up making all the difference?

The Hafley scheme was interesting, because it was mostly a scheme that disguised coverages, but didn’t do much on the pressure end, up until Micah Parsons came to town. When Parsons was on the field, teams obviously adjusted and ended up playing the Packers in more quick game and run game situations, which really forced Hafley to play more bland schemes—and Hafley went back to some “hidden” coverages once Parsons went down with an injury.

Gannon’s defense really has been about bringing pressure. He’ll send seven guys on the first play of the game without blinking, and the cornerbacks have been playing pretty well this year (all three safeties have been great). They’ve done some interesting things with individual teams’ pass-blocking rules to get free rushers. It’s not uncommon for Gannon to scheme up a pressure where there are seven blockers on four rushers, one of the rushers is a free rusher, and the Packers still have seven coverage players for just three route-runners.

The only time the defense hasn’t looked elite was against the Atlanta Falcons, which was a weird game. Bijan Robinson went crazy, and it seemed like everyone on both sides of the ball were slipping on the field that night other than Robinson. I think a lot of people are wondering if that was just a one-off or what the Packers’ defense looks like against a dynamic back. I think this week’s matchup will sort of answer that for us.

Hopefully, Micah Parsons will be a big addition down the line, yes. Please, God.

4. Green Bay lost Edgerrin Cooper for the season after he suffered a torn Achilles in Week 4. Who has Gannon called on to replace Cooper, and how have the Packers adjusted on defense since the injury? Have you noticed any shifting in personnel groupings/deployment without their star linebacker available?

EDITOR’S NOTE: This was asked and answered before Zaire Franklin suffered a mid-week injury and was declared out.

The Packers use their linebackers a lot on special teams, because LaFleur’s offensive players hardly play teams—outside of the return positions. So they have Zaire Franklin at the Mike position (he doesn’t play teams) and now the Will role (previously Cooper) is being split by Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper. My guess is they’re rotating McDuffie and Hopper (they change every two series or so) so that they can keep their legs fresh on special teams. Behind them, Green Bay rosters two linebackers who are functionally special teams-only players in Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch, if you want to know how important those linebackers are for the Packers’ special teams unit. Last week, they also called up Arron Mosby (a hybrid edge-linebacker who is basically another full-time special teamer) against the Cowboys.

Both McDuffie and Hopper have played well, but the linebackers have never really been tested (outside of the run game against Atlanta) this entire season. No one is really throwing over the middle against us, in part because we’re sending blitzers so much. It’s sort of hard to evaluate the position right now. In the moments when you would expect linebackers to be stressed by the passing game, that’s when Gannon is sending linebackers to go after the quarterback.

There hasn’t been a major shift in the Packers’ personnel packages since the Cooper injury. They are 99.7 percent match rate for 11 personnel in nickel right now. In heavier looks (12/13/21/22), they play their base 3-4 defense around 76 percent of the time. So if you want to keep Javon Bullard off the field for an extra nose tackle, play a second tight end.

5. The Packers opened as 3.5-point underdogs heading into this Week 7 matchup with the Lions, but that line has moved Green Bay’s way (+3) over at FanDuel Sportsbook. What’s one thing you want to see, what’s one thing you need to see, and one thing you’re sure you’ll see happen in this matchup between the Lions and Packers on Sunday afternoon?

One thing I want to see? Please show signs of life on the offensive line. One thing I want to see? The defensive line not getting worn down (we’re only rostering four defensive linemen currently on the 53-man roster, and the Dallas Cowboys decided to not run the ball and stay in 11 personnel last week) against the Lions’ offense. One thing I’m sure will happen? Points. I’ve seen your guys’ defensive numbers. Our corners have looked good so far this year, but we haven’t had to cover the likes of ARSB, Jamo, Gibbs and LaPorta all at the same time, plus we’re an aggressive unit. I wouldn’t be surprised if this game was decided by explosive haymakers.

item.title: Chicago Bears Week 7 Flashbacks: A GW Drive, NFL History, and More!
item.description: Hop aboard the Gridiron Time Machine with @iamcogs and take a trip down Week 7 Bears memory lane!
item.content:encoded:
Even though the Bears beat the Patriots on Thursday night, this time machine has no brakes! We’re back with three more games from Week 7 from Chicago Bears history. Hop aboard and enjoy this trip on the Gridiron Time Machine!

1. 2007, Bears @ Eagles: Griese engineers a 97-yard miracle

October 21, 2007 | Bears win 19-16

The defending NFC champions had stumbled to a 2-4 start in 2007, and things weren’t looking particularly promising in Philadelphia.

Chicago’s offense struggled to find the end zone for most of the afternoon, relying on four Robbie Gould field goals to keep pace with the Eagles.

When Donovan McNabb connected with Matt Schobel for a touchdown late in the fourth quarter, Philadelphia took a 16-12 lead.

The Bears eventually got the football back at their own three-yard line with 1:57 remaining, no timeouts, and needing a touchdown.

Enter Brian Griese.

With communication problems affecting his helmet headset, Griese called his own plays and marched Chicago 97 yards down the field. He connected with Bernard Berrian and Devin Hester on crucial completions before finding Muhsin Muhammad for a 15-yard touchdown with nine seconds remaining.

Griese finished with 322 passing yards and a touchdown, while Muhammad caught five passes for 79 yards.

Chicago escaped with a 19-16 victory, improving to 3-4 and keeping its postseason hopes alive.

2. 2017, Bears vs. Panthers: Eddie Jackson makes NFL history

October 22, 2017 | Bears win 17-3

Sometimes the defense doesn’t just help win a football game.

Sometimes it scores every touchdown.

That was the case when Carolina visited Soldier Field in Week 7 of the 2017 season.

Rookie safety Eddie Jackson wasted little time announcing himself.

On Carolina’s opening possession, Jackson scooped up a loose football and raced 75 yards for a touchdown. Early in the second quarter, he intercepted a deflected Cam Newton pass and returned it 76 yards for another score.

Just like that, Jackson had scored 14 points by himself.

He became the first player in NFL history to record two defensive touchdowns of at least 75 yards in the same game.

The Bears defense finished with three takeaways and five sacks, holding Carolina to just three points despite being outgained 293-153.

Perhaps the most ridiculous statistic from the afternoon belonged to Chicago’s offense.

Mitchell Trubisky completed just four passes for 107 yards, while the Bears managed only five first downs.

None of it mattered.

Chicago walked away with a 17-3 victory, improving to 3-4 and recording consecutive wins for the first time since 2015.

3. 2022, Bears @ Patriots: Chicago spoils Belichick’s historic opportunity

October 24, 2022 | Bears win 33-14

This one seems particularly appropriate with New England visiting Soldier Field Thursday night.

The Bears entered their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup in 2022 riding a three-game losing streak.

Meanwhile, Patriots coach Bill Belichick was sitting on 324 career victories, including the postseason, tied with Bears legend George Halas for second-most in NFL history.

A victory against Chicago would move Belichick past Papa Bear himself, but the Bears had other ideas.

Justin Fields had a solid game, completing 13-of-21 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown while rushing for another 82 yards and a score.

Chicago jumped out to a 10-0 lead before New England turned to backup quarterback Bailey Zappe, who briefly sparked the Patriots offense and gave them a 14-10 advantage.

That was the last time New England would score.

The Bears rattled off 23 unanswered points, rushing for 243 yards while forcing four turnovers, one of which forced by Spider-Man himself, rookie Kyler Gordon. Fields led the way on the ground, while David Montgomery and Khalil Herbert each contributed 62 rushing yards.

Cairo Santos added four field goals as Chicago cruised to a 33-14 victory.

The win was Chicago’s first in Foxborough and prevented Belichick from passing Halas in front of the franchise he helped build.

Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs.

The Saints are looking for their second consecutive win after surviving a furious comeback by the New York Giants last Sunday.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Steelers are -3 over the Saints at a neutral site. The current moneyline odds sit at -168 with an over/under of 44.5.

Here are three prop bets to target for Sunday morning:

Jaylen Warren anytime TD -120

Last week was frustrating, as Warren had several cracks at the end zone from the two-yard line, but failed to convert. Don’t let last week deter you from the free money this week. The Saints are one of the worst run defenses in the NFL, and Warren earned more touches down the stretch against the Bucs. He will still get the goal-line work, and the Steelers shouldn’t have trouble moving the football in Paris. Don’t overthink this one.

Aaron Rodgers over 0.5 rushing yards -140

Stay with me here. Rodgers has 19 rushing yards on the season. The old man has run for five yards (Week 2), ten yards (Week 3), and six yards (Week 5). The Saints’ pass rush is led by Chase Young, and the hope is that Rodgers scoots for a few yards to give himself breathing room for victory formation kneels. Let’s get dangerous, and this prop is easier to hit than it appears.

Germie Bernard over 53.5 receiving yards -114

Back-to-back games over 80 yards for the rookie should make this number very easy to hit. Bernard has nine and 12 targets in his last two games. This one is easy money, as it gets as Bernard will tangle with Jonas Sanker and potentially linebackers as defenders.

Putting all three picks together as a parlay gives you +475 odds. Ten dollars turns into a cool $47.56. Enjoy the game and let’s cash some slips.

item.title: NFL Week 7: 3 other games for Browns fans to keep an eye on
item.description: Week 7 has a few important games for Cleveland Browns fans, including AFC North action, and the Rams struggles
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the NFL season, with a win moving the visitors to 5-2 and a loss calling their early-season success into question. Injuries mean that any Saturday news from the Browns will be analyzed and scrutinized, including whether RB Dylan Sampson is activated from injured reserve. The bigger questions will be about practice squad elevations on defense, with CB Denzel Ward and LB Quincy Williams questionable for the game.

With Cleveland sitting at the top of the AFC North and fourth in the AFC playoff picture, there are a couple of games of importance going on around the league that they’ll want to watch. Two of the teams ahead of them in the playoff seeding, the Buffalo Bills (2nd seed) and Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd seed), have their byes this week, which limits the games of interest.

With the Los Angeles Rams owing the Browns their first-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft, “Rams Watch” is on every week, especially with injuries piling up and WR Puka Nacua questionable for Week 7.

With two AFC North teams facing off this week, that leaves just three vital games for Cleveland fans, besides their own, to watch in Week 7:

Steelers vs. Saints in Paris, early Sunday kickoff

The first game on Sunday, kicking off at 9:30 AM on NFL Network, is important for Browns fans for two reasons. First and obvious, the Pittsburgh Steelers are part of the AFC North and are tied for the best record in the division. Second, the Steelers and New Orleans Saints are Cleveland’s next two opponents.

The result of the game will be important, but watching to see how Pittsburgh’s energy is and any injuries coming during an international game could be a big deal for Week 8’s AFC North matchup. Last year, the Browns traveled to London the week before having to face the Steelers and looked lethargic after the long travel. The only difference this year is that Paris is a little further away than London, and Pittsburgh gets to play at home the next week, whereas Cleveland had to go on the road.

Bengals vs. Ravens at 1 PM

At the same time the Browns are playing, a pretty big matchup between the Cincinnati Bengals and Baltimore Ravens will be going on. The Bengals are in last place in the AFC North, at 3-2, and go on the road to face the Ravens, who should be getting QB Lamar Jackson back. Too early in the season for tiebreaker conversations; instead, fans will be rooting for a very physical game on the field.

item.title: 3 NFL Draft prospects of interest for the Bengals in College Football Week 8
item.description: The Bengals could look to one of these prospects for their left tackle of the future.
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore on Sunday this week, looking to improve to 4-2 on the season.

On Saturday, their eyes should be on some talented prospects across college football. While there are not a ton of top matchups like there were last week, it should still be another exciting week across the country.

Some of the top games this week include Texas vs. Ole Miss, Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt, and Utah vs. Houston. Let’s take a look at a few prospects that the Bengals could be scouting this week.

Lance Heard, LT, Kentucky

Heard transferred from Tennessee to Kentucky ahead of the 2026 season. The former five-star recruit has really taken a step forward in his development this season. The talent was always there, but he was so inconsistent the past couple of years for the Volunteers.

This year he has been the definition of consistency. He has allowed just 8 total pressures in 7 games played. The 6’6”, 325-pound left tackle has an 85.7 pass-blocking grade so far this season. He has a ton of experience playing tackle in the SEC. He has over 2,200 career snaps played already.

The Bengals gave Orlando Brown Jr. a two-year contract extension this offseason. His play has been up and down for most of the season, but he did play his best game of the year against the Dolphins. While left tackle might not ultimately be the biggest need come draft day, it should still be in consideration for Cincinnati. Brown will be turning 31 years old in May, and the dead money cap hit would only be $4.6 million dollars if they decide to let Brown go after the 2027 season.

Continuing to make sure that Joe Burrow is well protected should always be a priority.

Zereoue Williams, LT, Utah

I will stick with another talented left tackle prospect for the second player of note. Zereoue Williams had to wait his turn behind first-rounders Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu at Utah. That move is paying off for him this season. He has come out of nowhere to put himself firmly in the mix to be drafted in the first round.

Williams has ideal size at 6’8” and 315 pounds for an offensive tackle. His basketball background shows up consistently with how light he is on his feet. Williams has allowed just 3 pressures through 6 games played for Utah this season.

Williams didn’t play football from seventh grade until his senior season. The inexperience is certainly there since this is also his first full-time starting season at Utah. Instead of looking at that as purely a negative, I see a player with tremendous upside still. With what he is putting on tape already, this is a player that might have All-Pro potential at the next level.

Williams and the 10th-ranked Utah team will be going up against 14th-ranked Houston this week. It should be a fun matchup all around in Utah Saturday night.

Wayshawn Parker, RB, Utah

Chase Brown is set to be a free agent after this season in Cincinnati. He hasn’t exactly been lighting it up so far this season either. The Bengals could be in the market for a running back on draft day. My top running back prospect is Jadan Baugh from Florida. With his team on a bye, I think the Bengals should have their eyes on Wayshawn Parker from Utah.

Parker is in the conversation to be one of the next running backs drafted after Baugh this year. A likely Day 2 draft pick, Parker has already rushed for 597 yards this season. He is averaging a highly impressive 6.7 yards per carry, along with an insane 5.18 yards after contact per rushing attempt.

Parker can gain yards as a receiver, is one of the more elusive backs in the country, and he is much more physical than expected for a player who is listed at just 5’10” and 205 pounds. Parker has three-down potential at the next level and should be in the conversation for any team that wants to improve their rushing attack.

Who will you be watching today that you’d like to see on the Bengals next season?

item.title: Rams vs. Las Vegas Raiders: How to watch, start time, prediction and odds
item.description: Everything you need to know about the Rams facing the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, including start time, how to watch, injuries and betting odds.
item.content:encoded:
Another week, another Rams kicker.

On Sunday, veteran Brandon McManus will make his debut when the Rams play the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium.

McManus, 35, will be the third kicker — fourth if you count punter Ethan Evans’ extra-point cameo last Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals — to play this season for a Rams team that has stumbled, in part, because of kicking-game miscues.

The Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis two weeks ago and signed Blake Grupe, who made his first field-goal attempt against the Cardinals but suffered a season-ending knee injury in the ensuing kickoff when he knocked the returner out of bounds.

Read more:Puka Nacua questionable to play for Rams vs. Raiders; Nate Landman is out

The Rams summoned McManus and veteran Matt Prater to Woodland Hills for a tryout, and chose McManus after the workout.

“I’m a competitor and I love this game so much,” said McManus, who has played 12 seasons. “It’s done a lot for me and my family, so excited to get back out there and have that opportunity.”

McManus has made 297 of 362 field-goal attempts (82%) during stints with the Denver Broncos, Jacksonville Jaguars and Green Bay Packers. In 2025, he made 24 of 30 field-goal attempts for the Packers.

McManus said his experience with the Packers — in 2024 he joined them near midseason — would help him make a quick adjustment to the Rams and snapper Joe Cardona and holder Evans. He quipped that during his nine seasons with the Broncos, he worked with eight or nine punter/holders.

“So I’m used to seeing new things,” he said.

McManus is eager for his three sons to see him play.

Read more:Former Rams great Marshall Faulk shares Parkinson’s diagnosis, hopes to help others

“They get to watch me play on TV again,” he said. “They were young when I played most of my career, they didn’t really know. So now they’re older and their friends are talking at school, so it’s cool and exciting for them.”

Unlike the 5-foot-7, 156-pound Grupe, McManus is 6-3 and 201 pounds.

So his injury risk might be lower if he collides with a kick returner.

“I have double-digit tackles,” said McManus, who has 14.

Key injuries

Rams: LB Nate Landman (concussion, out); WR Puka Nacua (calf, questionable); CB Trent McDuffie (groin, questionable)

Raiders: TE Carter Runyon (foot, out); WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring, out); RB Mike Washington (foot/back, questionable).

How to watch and listen to Rams vs. Raiders

The Rams and Las Vegas Raiders will play Sunday at 1:25 p.m. PDT at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. The game will be shown throughout California on Fox. It will be available nationally via a subscription to NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV. In Southern California, fans can listen to the game on 710 AM and 1330 AM (Español).

Betting lines and odds for Rams vs. Raiders

Who will win Rams vs. Raiders?

The Rams are depleted by injuries, but they still have enough talent — if Nacua plays — to outlast a Raiders team that started 3-0 but has lost its last three games.

Gary Klein’s pick: Rams 27, Raiders 24

item.title: Injury-marred Rams don't want your sympathy. They're out to prove they can save their season
item.description: The Rams will face the Las Vegas Raiders with several players out because of injuries, but the team sees it as an opportunity to shine through adversity.
item.content:encoded:
Still a lot of games left.

No one is panicking.

Been in this position before.

Those are affirmations Rams players and coaches have utilized during a season of great expectations mired in major underachievement.

The Rams, who opened the season as the Super Bowl favorite, will arrive in Las Vegas for Sunday’s game against the Raiders with a 2-4 record and a two-game losing streak.

And they will be without several key players counted on to reverse their fortunes.

Star receiver Davante Adams is out — and is expected to be sidelined five to nine more weeks because of a hamstring injury. Star receiver Puka Nacua, who suffered a calf injury this week in practice, will be a game-time decision.

Defensive lineman Kobie Turner was placed on injured reserve this week because of a groin injury, joining edge rusher Myles Garrett, who has been sidelined since the season-opening defeat by the San Francisco 49ers following knee surgery. Defensive tackle Poona Ford this week was declared out for the season because of a triceps injury.

Linebacker Nate Landman won’t play against the Raiders because of a concussion, and All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable because of a groin injury.

Meantime, the NFC West-rival San Francisco 49ers are 6-0, and the Rams are last in the division.

The Rams and coach Sean McVay have turned around seasons before. In 2023 and 2024 they overcame slow starts to win 10 games and make the playoffs.

“You can’t sit there and go, ‘Because we did X, we’re going to do Y,’ but we obviously know what it takes to win football games,” quarterback Matthew Stafford said. “We can’t sit there and look at the big picture and go, ‘OK, we have X amount of games left. These guys are doing that,’ or whatever.

“That’s not the mindset at all around here.”

The Rams have their own concerns, most notably a receiving corps that will be without Adams and possibly Nacua.

Read more:How a clash between Inglewood leaders and SoFi Stadium operators hit the ballot

Adams, 33, is a three-time All-Pro and probable future Hall of Famer.

“You’re not going to one-for-one sub in a guy that’s going to be wearing a gold jacket one day, in Davante,” Stafford said. “It’s a team effort.”

It became an even more urgent one Thursday when Nacua was unable to finish practice.

Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, rookie CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman are other receivers on the roster.

“Whether you’re talking about Davante, whether you’re talking about Puka, you don’t ever ask anybody to replace those guys,” McVay said, adding, “I want those players to be their best selves. ... It’s a great opportunity for other guys to step up if that’s the situation that we’re dealing with.”

Atwell, Mumpfield and Whittington have combined for only 13 receptions. This could be the first game Daniels will be active.

“We’re all held to a certain standard,” Whittington said. “When you are held to that standard, I think the drop-off shouldn’t be that big. We all have a culture we abide by and everybody displays and embodies that. And I think it will work how it needs to work.”

McVay also could rely more heavily on running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, and tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen.

“It’s not any more pressure to anyone on the team,” Williams said.

With Turner and Ford sidelined, the Rams’ interior defensive front will include Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis, Larrell Murchison and Ty Hamilton.

Donald, who ended a two-year retirement to rejoin the Rams, is averaging just over 38 snaps a game.

Will that role grow?

Read more:Puka Nacua questionable to play for Rams vs. Raiders; Nate Landman is out

“We have a general snap count that he’s always going to have going into the game,” defensive coordinator Chris Shula said. “I don’t think we would go crazily past that, but it’s going to be hard if it’s a tight game and he’s at that number.

“Just like one of those pitchers in the ninth inning, you’re probably going to leave him in for a few extra snaps.”

Said Donald: “If it’s 30 plays, 40 plays, 50 plays, 60 plays, that’s what it’s going to be.”

The Rams have 11 games remaining, including Sunday’s against the Raiders, a home game against the Chargers and road games at Washington and Arizona before their bye week.

“It’s not over,” Donald said. “Is there a sense of urgency? For sure, because we want to win.

“But as far as curling up and panicking like this is the end of the world, it’s not that. We have a lot of ball to play, a lot of games left.”

item.title: Commanders fans choose patience over panic with Dan Quinn & look ahead to a wide-open NFC East
item.description: A 1-4-1 start hasn’t killed hope, with 64% of fans backing Jayden Daniels and the Commanders for a second-half division push
item.content:encoded:
In this week’s Reacts survey, we asked Hogs Haven readers two questions regarding the state of the Washington Commanders as the team enters its Week 7 bye.

A question of confidence

The first question was our standard pulse check: Are you confident in the team’s direction?

  • No: 74%
  • Yes: 26%

Interestingly, that 26% positive mark represents an 8-point jump from the 18% registered after Week 6 despite the Commanders suffering a second consecutive loss. While nearly three-quarters of the fanbase remains skeptical—understandably so after a grueling 1-4-1 start—the modest uptick suggests that a few days of distance from game action have allowed a little bit of perspective to seep back in.

What Hogs Haven readers want to see from the team after the bye

Our second question tackled the immediate road ahead: What do you want to see from the Commanders after the bye week?

  • Rally around Dan Quinn, fight to win games, and reach the postseason: 64%
  • An interim head coach to replace Dan Quinn and a shift in focus to the 2027 season: 36%

Taken together, the results of the two survey questions tell a revealing story about where this fanbase stands at the mid-autumn break. While 3 out of 4 fans remain uneasy with the broader direction after six weeks of frustration, nearly two-thirds flatly reject the idea of waving a white flag on the 2026 campaign. There is a tangible difference between acknowledging a disappointing start and surrendering to it, and Hogs Haven readers clearly believe that letting Dan Quinn and this squad fight through the storm offers a far better path forward than triggering an organizational fire drill in late October.

The case for measured optimism in the “second season” that starts after the bye

To anyone staring strictly at the standings, talking about a postseason push might sound borderline delusional. The bad news from the first 6 weeks is well known, painful to recount, and needs little rehash here: missed opportunities, fourth-quarter breakdowns, and an offense that was severely hindered when quarterback injuries disrupted Weeks 2, 3, and 4.

Yet, nearly two-thirds of our readers voted against pulling the rip cord. As Alex Rowsey aptly put it in the comments, it is hard to stomach punting on an NFL season when the NFC East remains completely up for grabs.

Look around the neighborhood. The Philadelphia Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, have dropped 4 straight games, and look vulnerable heading into the Week 8 road game against Washington. The Dallas Cowboys, despite avoiding the quarterback injuries that partly-derailed Washington’s early slate, have also dropped 4 of their first 6 games and look just as out of sorts. Meanwhile, the New York Giants sit just 2 games ahead of Washington and enter this weekend as double-digit underdogs against the Houston Texans.

Nobody is running away with this division. In fact, Washington’s remaining strength of schedule over the final 11 games is among the easiest in the NFL, which seems to open up a world of opportunity – if the team can make some meaningful improvements during this week’s lull in the action.

The secret ingredient to success

Most importantly, Jayden Daniels has played high-caliber football behind center and continues to display significant upside. As offensive coordinator David Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones gain comfort and rhythm in their play-calling duties, the units around Daniels should improve steadily. If the coaching staff utilizes the bye week to incorporate more quick reads, rhythmic RPOs, and enhanced and aggressive defensive looks—points raised repeatedly by commenters and media—this team has plenty of room for meaningful growth.

Dan Quinn, Josh Harris, and the executive reality

In addition to the Reacts surveys we carry out on Hogs Haven, SB Nation conducts regular weekly national (even international) polling of fans across the fanbases of all 32 teams via email. This week, one of the national survey questions asked which coach would be the first to be fired this season.

Visit our partners at FanDuel

I think the national press and most NFL fans are reading the situation in Washington all wrong. It seems to me that a hell of a lot more would have to go wrong for the Washington ownership group to consider parting ways with DQ in the midst of his 3rd season.

It’s true that a sizable 36% contingent voted for an interim coach to replace Quinn in our Reacts survey this week, and several commenters made thoughtful arguments about clock management and late-game execution. But owner Josh Harris is an experienced professional sports owner who understands the value of organizational stability. Harris knows all too well the damage caused by knee-jerk, emotional reactions to early-season adversity.

There is an old, reliable axiom in professional management that applies to both business and sports: a good executive supports his guy 100% right up until the exact moment he doesn’t.

That is not an empty cliché; it is how professional organizations operate — and Josh Harris knows how to run a professional organization. As long as Dan Quinn is the head coach of the Washington Commanders, he holds the complete, undivided support of ownership. Harris has shown throughout his ownership career that he prefers to evaluate a full body of work across an entire 17-game campaign rather than pulling the plug mid-stream. Quinn will be given every opportunity to navigate through these waters, and I would hope that fans will be pulling for him to succeed — our survey results indicate that most Hogs Haven readers will absolutely continue to root for the team to win games and earn a playoff spot. Personally, I expect Quinn to succeed in turning the 2026 season around, and I expect him to remain the head coach into 2027 after doing so.

Consistent leadership and direction over a period of years has been proven to be more effective in the NFL than constantly lurching from one vision of leadership to another based on short term results. With 11 games left to play in the 2026 season, there’s a lot of time left to right the ship, but that opportunity would be lost if the mob mentality of “fire everyone” were to be adopted by Harris because of a tough few weeks to open the season.

Charting the path back to relevance

If you are looking for a reasonable roadmap to a season turnaround, consider how the next month sets up.

Coming out of the bye, the Commanders face a wounded Philadelphia team, followed by the 2-4 Rams, and then a rematch with the Giants (who’ve  just made the QB switch to JJ McCarthy). Winning those 3 games is entirely within reach, and doing so would vault Washington to 4-4-1, putting them right back at the .500 mark with 8 games to play.

From there, the schedule remains exceptionally favorable. Winning 4 of the 6 winnable games between Weeks 11 and 16 (Bengals, Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons, Vikings) would have Washington sitting two games above .500 heading into a pivotal Week 17 clash in Jacksonville.

With one of the easiest remaining schedules in football ahead of them, the Commanders could put together a string of victories reminiscent of the 2012 Redskins (from 3-6, 7 straight wins to close out the season) or the 2015 team (from 2-4, 6 wins in the final 8 games; 7 wins in the final 10). Heck, even the 2020 Football Team won a division title in a weak NFC East by going 5-2 in the final 7 games after a 2-7 start.

We’ve seen the burgundy & gold turn mid-season losing teams into division champions three times in recent years; all of the ingredients seem to be in place for the same thing to happen in 2026 — hopefully, though, with more postseason success than the 2012, 2015 & 2020 division champions enjoyed. With Jayden Daniels healthy and playing, postseason success like 2024 is possible to achieve again if the team can do what is required now to reach the playoffs in January.

Washington’s next game

The first 6 weeks of 2026 tested everyone’s patience, but the franchise has been here before, and the ‘second season’ begins on Sunday Night Football in Week 8 when the Commanders host the Eagles at Northwest Stadium at 8:20 pm.

Currently, the Commanders are favored by 3.5 points at home against the Eagles, with an over/under of 40.5 points.

Let’s hope this is the first giant step towards another notable mid-season turnaround and a successful postseason campaign!

item.title: The Broncos aren’t overlooking the Cardinals
item.description: The Denver Broncos aren’t underestimating the Arizona Cardinals yet believe this can be the game where everything begins to click for them.
item.content:encoded:
After their first six games of the 2026 season, the Denver Broncos find themselves in familiar territory. They sport a 4-2 record—just like last season. It wasn’t pretty then and hasn’t been thus far. Nevertheless, more wins than losses is always a good thing.

Strong defensive performances and penchant for fourth quarter heroics have continued for this year’s Broncos. This weekend, they face off against the Arizona Cardinals who are currently 2-4 and coming off an impressive victory the Los Angeles Rams. Even though the Cardinals have a losing record, the Broncos aren’t overlooking their Week 7 opponent.

Each game provides an opportunity for every team in the National Football League. For the Broncos this Sunday, it’s a chance to get an important fifth win of the season. Moreover, it could become a streak starter. A gridiron battle—if won—that would give them confidence and momentum as the second half of the season approaches.

Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton touched based on a variety of topics. However, finding a way to improve and string together more victories to go on a run [like last year] was a point of emphasis.

“That 4-2 mark a year ago, we’d come off of a real good defensive effort in London. It just can’t be a yo-yo. Any team that I can think of, there are runs. I think more importantly the last thing I just said to them was, ‘We have to be ascending, improving.’ I think they understand that,” stated Payton.

The Broncos haven’t played a complete game thus far. Interestingly enough quite similar to 2025. The major exception being the matchup versus the Cincinnati Bengals who were without star quarterback Joe Burrow. There is no doubt Payton’s right. Denver needs to keep pushing forward and make the necessary adjustments to become a more complete team that’s built to compete for the long haul.

A huge part of that is finding a viable recipe for success offensively. Broncos Country has grown accustomed to slowing starts on offense the past several years, only to find relief in the second half of the season when things finally started to click. Though with a little extra preparation for their Week 7 matchup, the team hopes that spark comes sooner than later.

The Cardinals may not have a lot of star power on defense and rank in the bottom half of most metrics across the board. However, they put together a quality outing against the Los Angeles Rams last weekend. They give a lot of different looks and switch up a lot between Cover 3, Cover 4, and Cover 6 coverage looks—zone principles that Bo Nix and Denver’s offense are failing to find ways to beat.

In order for the offense to do better, Payton acknowledged that it will be critical to be able to decipher and adequately react to their unique defensive packages.

“Our defense, we see a base-look, kind of an Okie structure. There’ll be some similarities. Then they have a nickel package, a dime. Their penny—and we have a penny too—it can be a little blurry. One of the important notes this week was Communication ID,” mentioned Payton.

“Usually there’s someone in the huddle that’s looking, and Bo is stepping into the huddle. They’re saying, ‘Nickel, nickel,’ or ‘Base, base.’ Then I’ll a lot of times say, ‘Hey Bo, this is base defense here.’ When we’re game planning, if you’re wanting to run a play against their base defense, there are certain things in order to know you’re getting base. There’s no 100 percent. That’s an important thing this week,” added Payton.

How the Broncos choose to combat Arizona’s defense will be interesting to watch. Everyone is hoping to see Nix dial it up through the air, yet the biggest weakness the Cardinals have defensively is stopping the run. They’ve given up over 140 yards in three contests thus far.

I think a big part of their game plan will be a healthy dose of J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey, and giving reps to Jonah Coleman who is expected to play on Sunday. If Denver can establish a formidable rushing attack, that would bode well for Nix and the offense, who have thrived off play-action principles and deep shots when the running game is clicking.

Can Denver’s offense finally find a recipe for success on Sunday? You’ll just have to tune in and find out.

item.title: Rewriting the Narrative: The Vikings’ New Story
item.description: Words are words
item.content:encoded:
Narrative is a funny thing in the NFL. Sometimes I question where all of the different storylines come from or why the media focuses on certain aspects over others. Not to be a conspiracy theorist (even though it’s sometimes a hobby for me), but I am sure the NFL marketing department sends information out to certain insiders to cover the stories they want to be prevailing storylines. Maybe that’s not true, but there are no definitive facts that could convince me that there isn’t a possibility that most NFL storylines portrayed in the mainstream media are contrived from somewhere inside an NFL VP or executive suite.

A new narrative that could pick up steam after this weekend is that the Vikings “chose the wrong quarterback.” People are losing their minds over J.J. McCarthy coming into a game in the fourth quarter, down by 24 points, and leading a feverish comeback that ultimately felt short. It looked all too familiar to Vikings’ fans. For some reason, J.J. McCarthy has always thrived in the 4th quarter. The narrative that is already forming is that Kevin O’Connell’s system wasn’t right for McCarthy and that things are simplified in John Harbaugh’s offense. While that may be true, I didn’t see anything on Sunday that leads me to believe that McCarthy will find any more success in New York than he did in Minnesota.

Jason LaCanfora is reporting that some New York Giants executive says there is going to be a major shift in offensive philosophy for New York and to look at the 2018 Ravens with Lamar Jackson in his rookie season. Apparently, New York has been eyeing McCarthy for quite some time to bring in as their starting quarterback. I find that slightly far-fetched based on them only willing to trade a 5th-round pick to acquire him. If McCarthy finds success in New York, there will be questions about why he didn’t find success in Minnesota.

Persevere Toward Excellence

I know what you’re thinking: STOP TALKING ABOUT THE NEW YORK GIANTS. I am, right now. Narrative lives in a world of hypotheticals. We live in the real world. Reality cannot be denied, and the Vikings are 5-0 going into a very winnable game against the Indianapolis Colts. The Minnesota Vikings have started a season with a 6-0 record six times in the modern NFL era. Of those six seasons, they made the playoffs in all but one, which was in 2003 when they lost on the last play of the season to the Arizona Cardinals. The game that culminated in the classic Paul Allen screaming “NOOOOOOOOO.”

All these narratives can be squashed if Kyler Murray goes out and performs to the level at which he is capable. The experiment of drafting a first-round quarterback is over, and we are officially under the Nolan Teasley regime. Minnesota knew what they had in McCarthy. Maybe the Giants were willing to give more in a trade, but the narrative that I am choosing to perpetuate is that the front office was simply ready to move on and was satisfied getting any value back. I wish J.J. the best, but the franchise has chosen a new path.

That is what I will do here as well and move on. The Minnesota Vikings are the most enigmatic team in the NFL. Some armchair NFL analysts (people on social media who bought a microphone and know how to post on the internet) are saying that the Vikings are the third-best team in the NFC North. They’re not calling us the third-best 5-0 team; they are saying that the Bears and Packers (both of whom we beat with Carson Wentz) are better. HA!

Are We Witnessing History?

This defense is special. Like really special, as evidenced by how the Vikings’ current 10-game win streak has manifested itself. Over the last 10 games, the Minnesota Vikings have scored 229 points. Historically, you have to go back to 1934 to find a 10-game winning streak where the team scored fewer points (the 1934 Detroit Lions scored 215 points). That is an astonishing statistic but speaks to the dominance that we have seen from this defense. Football is about winning games. Sure, the Vikings offense has had its struggles and is still finding its footing. Is that a circumstance of poor coaching or them being a bad offense? Or is it a result of a shift in philosophy for Kevin O’Connell?

From a narrative perspective, KO is rewriting the defining story of his time as the coach of the Minnesota Vikings. He recently talked about how he has shifted his mindset from being concerned with what stats look like on paper to winning football games. This team is playing complementary football at its finest. Every season has its ebbs and flows, but we also see those differences happen over the course of multiple seasons. Right now, the defense is obviously the strength of this team. When Brian Flores’ unit is fresh, they are almost unstoppable. One thing I have noticed is just how relentless the defensive front is. They just keep coming and don’t stop until after the whistle. The defense is playing with such an intensity that it simply wears down opposing offenses and beats them down into submission.

Gotta Have the Ball to Score

An important factor in this success is the offense’s ability to maintain drives. So far this season, the Vikings’ are averaging the second highest average time of possession in the league at 33:38 per game. They trail only the Chicago Bears in this category. I will concede that the Vikings haven’t been very efficient when it comes to scoring touchdowns, but I firmly believe that is going to change. In fantasy football, we talk about regression toward the mean. The Minnesota offense has only scored eight offensive touchdowns in 5 games played this season, which is the 2nd fewest in the league. However, this offense is better than that, and we will start to see that number look more normal going forward.

Another prevailing shift in philosophy is that this now appears to be a run-first offense, as evidenced by the aforementioned time of possession statistic. This offense is about controlling the clock and taking care of the football. It’s like we are time traveling back to the Mike Zimmer era. However, this is the Teasley/O’Connell/Flores era. We are fans of one of the premier organizations in the NFL, and I think we are going to actually see success beyond the regular season. I know, as a Vikings fan, hope is a slippery slope. A slippery slope to sadness and disappointment.

There Is a Long Road Ahead

The game this Sunday against the Colts will set the tone for the rest of the season. I fully expect Indianapolis, with their backs to the wall, to make this game competitive for as long as they can. I can also see Daniel Jones throwing four interceptions, which would squash a different narrative that the Vikings shouldn’t have let him leave the building. I think Minnesota wins this game in dominant fashion, and we see our offense come to life. They are going to have to, because this team has a tough schedule going forward where they are going to have to put some points on the board. It’s time for this offense to get rolling and for the defense to keep doing what it does. I can’t wait for Sunday!

Until Next Skol.

The Dallas Cowboys are averaging less than 80 yards a game running the football, and they need to get it going somehow against a tough Philadelphia Eagles defense. Mike Pettine provides a ton of experience to the Cowboys, and they hope it spreads throughout the entire coaching staff.

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson says Bears' defensive alignment helped with 48-yard TD
item.description: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears. Stevenson said the Bears' defensive alignment made it possible.

The Bears were so concerned about giving up a Hail Mary on the last play of the half that they put two defensive backs near the goal line, almost 50 yards downfield. The Bears also rushed six to try to prevent Patriots quarterback Drake Maye from having time to set up for a Hail Mary. But that meant the middle of the field was wide open.

"It's kind of how they lined up pre-snap that got us into that play," Stevenson said.

The Bears' defense seemed to be caught off-guard, not expecting Maye to dump it off to Stevenson only a yard past the line of scrimmage. And it's not surprising the Bears weren't expecting it, as scoring a touchdown in that situation is almost unheard of: According to Doug Clawson of CBS Sports, there have been 1,006 plays in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, starting more than 40 yards from the end zone, in which the ball was thrown less than 10 yards downfield, and Stevenson's catch was the only one of those 1,006 plays that turned into a touchdown.

"I was just trying to make a play, put my team in a position to swing the game a little bit, as much as we can," Stevenson said. "We've been working on that play for a long time and it came in handy today. Executed on that play so it felt good to do that."

Asked what his mindset was when Maye threw him the Ball, Stevenson answered, "Score."

He did that, producing one of the best touchdowns of this NFL season.

The Bengals trio has continued to get better and better each season, and Tee Higgins has taken another step in 2026.

Higgins currently has 27 catches for 423 yards and a touchdown through the Bengals’ first 5 games, but he has been exceptional in one specific category.

Higgins currently lives in a world of his own against man coverage so far this season.

item.title: College Players to Watch: Week 7
item.description: Here are some players to keep an eye on in Week 7 and why they would matter to the Saints.
item.content:encoded:
While the New Orleans Saints are preparing to take on the Steelers in Paris tomorrow morning, there are some intriguing college players to watch on Saturday who could potentially become additions to the Saints’ roster in 2027.

Here are three college players to watch this Saturday.

Cam Coleman, WR, Texas

Yes, a wide receiver.

The likelihood of this happening is very low, but Coleman is still an exciting player to watch. He will be matching up against a very talented Ole Miss team tonight at 6:30 PM on ABC.

Coleman and quarterback Arch Manning are still looking to make the Texas offense more explosive, but Coleman’s combination of size, speed, athleticism, and ability to make contested catches makes him one of the best receivers in the class.

Suntarine Perkins, EDGE/OLB, Ole Miss

Perkins will be on the field at the same time as Cam Coleman, and if the Texas offense is sputtering, there’s a good chance it will be because of the impact Perkins is having on Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorn offense.

Perkins possesses the ability to rush the passer and play off-ball linebacker. His versatility would be a welcome addition to a Saints defense looking for a consistent complement to Chase Young, as well as a player who can operate off the ball and make plays in space.

Justin Scott, DT, Miami

The No. 1 team in the nation will take on Pitt at 11 AM on ESPN, and in the middle of Miami’s defense will be Justin Scott.

Scott is a powerful interior defensive tackle who can play well against the run and affect the quarterback from the interior.

This has been a major issue for the Saints’ defensive front this season. Not having a consistent presence in the heart of the defensive line has negatively affected the Saints’ run defense while also allowing opposing quarterbacks more time to step up in the pocket and find open receivers downfield.

The Saints have a lot of issues, so adding talent at almost any position this offseason would be a breath of fresh air.

Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to battle the Houston Texans this Sunday.

Struggles in all three phases leave Giants feeling heat heading into matchup at Texans | The Athletic

The New York Giants’ coaching staff turned up the heat this week. It started after Sunday’s 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints when coach John Harbaugh challenged someone from a disappointing backfield to step up and seize the top running back job.

Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy noted that the coaches need to look inward as the team searches for solutions to their weaknesses. One area that falls under the coaches’ purview is penalties. The Giants have been flagged for the 13th-most penalties in the league. They have the most pre-snap offensive penalties, lowlighted by consecutive false starts on running back Tyrone Tracy and left tackle Andrew Thomas to turn a third-and-8 into a third-and-18 in the third quarter against the Saints.

Giants’ Matt Nagy ready to open up playbook for J.J. McCarthy’s first start | New York Post

“Maybe now 20 percent of that 30 that was gone is back,” Nagy said. “For us, what does he do well? You’ve seen some of the packages he’s done, but that can become predictable. We don’t want to be predictable. Now that he’s the starter, it probably benefits us some that he’s just not always coming in to do predictable QB-driven runs.” 

“Just the confidence of him being able to, in practice, talk to us about the scheme, where his eyes are going in the pass game, where he’s snapping the ball with a motion or a shift,” Nagy said.  “If there was a shoestring with Jameis or he got hurt, he could go in and function. Whereas the first two weeks, I had a highlighted [play] call sheet that, if something happened and he was in, these were the plays. It was probably 50 percent. Last week, it was probably 90 percent. Now this week, it’s going to be 100 percent.” 

Harbs Weekly: A chance to take control of the division before the bye week | Giants.com

Q: A lot of times we see quarterback changes made at the bye week, which is coming up. But if something is inevitable, is it best to do it as soon as possible because now you get this week too?

I’m just thinking about what was the best thing for the next game and was he ready. It really wasn’t all that. I mean, it’s good to think about. Now that people have brought it up, I’m like, I didn’t really care about that.

Harbaugh on the release of Najee Harris

Colts’ Jonathan Taylor to Giants? Why Cam Skattebo knows he shouldn’t rule it out | NJ.com

Giants coach John Harbaugh wants a dominant, single-back running game, as he chases an unlikely NFC East title this season. Really, that also is Harbaugh’s broader vision for his offense in East Rutherford.

So Cam Skattebo — who entered his second year as the Giants’ much-hyped but largely unproven No. 1 back — knows he can’t and shouldn’t rule out Harbaugh trading for the Colts’ Jonathan Taylor (a New Jersey native) prior to the Nov. 10 deadline.

New York Giants’ skill players call for improved run-game execution | USAToday.com

Nabers said the offense must do a better job establishing the run so defenses cannot simply play the pass on every down.
