item.title: Bears lead NFL in time of possession, but Ben Johnson would prefer one-play TD drives
item.description: ""I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing," Johnson said.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears lead the NFL in time of possession, but that doesn't matter to coach Ben Johnson.

"I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing, necessarily. And yet when you look up, we were possessing the ball more than our opponent more often than not," Johnson said.

The Bears' average time of possession of 35:30 per 60-minute game is the highest in the NFL, they've run 505 offensive plays this season, which is by far the most of any team, and they're the only team averaging more than 70 offensive plays per game. Johnson said he thinks about how long drives affect players, both on offense and defense, but that he's ultimately happier when his offense scores quickly than slowly.

"It's not something that we stress," Johnson said. "We really talk more about getting explosive plays. I would rather have a one-play drive for a touchdown than a 10-play drive for a touchdown. But the ability to stay efficient, stay on schedule, I think that's something that good offenses show that they can do."

The Bears have shown they're a good offense, even if sometimes it takes them longer to get into the end zone than Johnson would like.

item.title: Jalyx Hunt explains relief of knowing his season didn't end in London
item.description: Jalyx Hunt avoided major injury in London and is looking forward to getting back to game action.
item.content:encoded:
Jalyx Hunt explains relief of knowing his season didn't end in London originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jalyx Hunt was scared.

His left leg just got caught under him and he heard a pop. So you can imagine the fear that ran through him as he laid on the field at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium a couple weeks ago.

“Terrifying,” Hunt said. “I haven’t experienced an injury like that before in my football career. Thank God I can say that. I heard a pop, went down like that, felt how awkward the position was, knowing that’s not a normal position for your body to be in. It was really scary.

“And then having to get that X-ray at the field and feeling how I was feeling, it was scary. I had to call the people, let them know I was OK. Had the prayer warriors out. Mom was praying for me, dad was praying. So, yeah, real scary.”

If you understand the fear Hunt felt in that moment, you can also probably understand the relief he felt when he realized he was going to be OK. Hunt missed the Panthers game last week with knee and ankle injuries but was already back on the practice field this week. 

Whether or not he plays on Monday night, at least this wasn’t a season-ending injury.

“Shout out God,” Hunt said. “Shout out the fact that I do yoga and pilates in the offseason.”

Hunt, 25, credited his flexibility as a reason he was able to walk away from an awkward position others wouldn’t have escaped without serious injury. Hunt was on the turf in London for long after the first half ended, but then he waved off the cart.

On Thursday, Hunt said his group chat talked about that move this week, and his teammates said they would have given him crap if he accepted the ride.

“I don’t know what it is, maybe it’s an unwritten rule,” Hunt said. “But I’m only taking that cart if I physically cannot walk or I feel as if the season’s over. I felt like I had the strength enough to at least hobble off, so I was going to do it. That cart off, man, I’ve seen some nasty things happen. Nah, I didn’t want to be along with that group.”

Sunday’s game against the Panthers was the first game Hunt has missed because of injury in his NFL career. Hunt was actually a healthy scratch in Week 1 of his rookie season in 2024 but had played in every game since then.

So it was weird to be standing on the sideline against the Panthers.

“Oh it sucked,” Hunt said. “I was trying to bring energy from the sideline. Can’t really do too much.”

And then to make matters worse, Nolan Smith went down with a concussion and Jonathan Greenard’s ankle began acting up. That meant that Arnold Ebiketie smashed his career-high in defensive snaps with 72. And Keyshawn James-Newby, in his NFL debut, played 48 snaps on defense. In addition to their roles on defense, Ebiketie played 12 snaps on special teams and James-Newby played 9 on special teams.

That’s a lot for both of them.

“I felt bad putting that workload on them and thank God I’m in a great room where everybody is just a dawg,” Hunt said. “But it felt real bad not being able to contribute and help the team.”

Hunt isn’t sure if he’ll be able to make his return against the Cowboys on Monday night. He obviously wants to play, but he’s trying to put his faith in the trainers and medical staff.

He was limited to start the week.

“It sucked not being able to contribute,” Hunt said, “but at the same time, I would hate to come back and not be ready and be a detriment to the team when we have more than capable people in the room. It is an added motivation but I wouldn’t make that the main focus just because I wouldn’t want to put my team behind simply from a selfish act of wanting to play football again when there’s people who are healthy and willing and more able than I am.”

item.title: Makai Lemon facing big opportunity in huge game vs. Cowboys
item.description: Eagles rookie Makai Lemon will have a big opportunity on Monday night against the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Makai Lemon facing big opportunity in huge game vs. Cowboys originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Dallas Goedert (knee) have missed practice this week and their availability for Monday night against the Cowboys is in question.

So this could be a big moment for Makai Lemon.

The rookie first-round pick has had solid moments through the first six weeks of the season. But as the Eagles get ready to face the Cowboys a little short-handed, they’re going to have to rely on Lemon.

“Definitely a big opportunity for the team,” Lemon said. “Just super excited to go out there with the guys and put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys so just trying to go out there and execute. Like you said, a couple guys are out so really just next man up. 

“I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trusting the coaches and the game plan. So I’m definitely excited for this week’s matchup.”

The Eagles (2-4) are hosing the Cowboys (2-4) on Monday night in a game with huge ramifications in the NFC East. It’s a big moment for Lemon and the team.

Through six games, the 22-year-old Lemon has played 72% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps and has 18 catches on 28 targets for 127 yards. His production isn’t great right now but Lemon has looked much better when the Eagles aren’t tossing him passes behind the line of scrimmage.

The last couple of weeks, Lemon has been learning how to play with backup quarterback Tanner Mckee, who has taken over for Jalen Hurts. The Eagles’ starting QB is expected to miss the rest of the season after blood clots were found in his lungs and McKee is now the guy.

That’s just one chapter in what has been a wild story for the Eagles’ 2026 season. It has been a pretty crazy rookie season for Lemon.

“It’s definitely been a lot of curveballs, a lot of things that I wouldn’t expect my first year,” Lemon said. “But I feel like just taking everything as a learning experience, learn from everything that comes my way. And just leaning on the guys around me that have been in the league, that have done this multiple times before. Especially in my room, we got a lot of veteran guys around me. So just leaning on them, talking to them and going out and just playing ball really.”

If Smith and Wicks can’t play on Monday against the Cowboys, the Eagles’ top receivers will be Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Hollywood Brown. Lemon is the only normal starter in that group.

The No. 20 overall pick from USC hasn’t been having an incredible rookie season but he does feel himself improving in ways that might not show up on the stat sheet. He said on Friday that his comfort in this offense has grown a lot. He wants to learn it like the back of his hand, so he doesn’t have to think as much on the field.

And even after some rough moments for Lemon earlier this season, the rookie has remained very confident.

“I feel I got great confidence, definitely,” Lemon said. “I get a lot of my confidence just from the work that I put in.”

item.title: You're not the only one wondering why the Eagles haven't used Hollywood Brown
item.description: Brown has no targets through Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
You're not the only one wondering why the Eagles haven't used Hollywood Brown originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

No catches, no targets, one game, 17 snaps.

That’s the sum total of the first six weeks of Hollywood Brown’s Eagles career.

The former 1st-round pick, who’s averaged over 700 yards in six healthy NFL seasons, expected more when he signed here. 

“I did, but I do understand stuff happens,” Brown said at his locker Friday. “I mean, you can’t take anything personal in this business, so you kind of just got to go about your process and when that time happens, whatever happens, you’ve just got to be ready for it.”

Not an easy lesson to learn and one that took Brown a while to learn.

“Definitely just being older and being in the league for a minute,” he said. “I wouldn’t have handled it as well as a younger guy, but now just knowing I’m blessed to be here. I can’t be mad about a situation because maybe that’s not what God called for me.”

Brown had a 90-catch, 1,000-yard season with the Ravens in 2021. He also surpassed 700 yards in 2020 and 2022 and has been over 500 yards every other full year of his career. He has 33 touchdown catches since 2019 and that’s with missing all of 2024.

But so far this year? Nothing. Hasn’t even had a football thrown his way.

“It’s just really taking it day by day,” he said. “I just really have to be right when I get my opportunity, so that’s what I’ve been focused on.”

Brown signed a one-year, $5 million contract with the Eagles in free agency, so you would expect him to have a bigger role. 

Why hasn’t it worked out that way?

“Honestly, I don’t have an answer,” he said with a smile. “I don’t know, but what I can do is just try to be ready and go from there. I feel like I’m putting good stuff on tape (at practice). But I could be playing and still not getting the ball or I could be playing and getting the ball and we’re losing. So I try not to make it all about me and just try to roll with the punches.”

It’s possible the Eagles will be without both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks for their Monday night game against the Cowboys at the Linc. Neither has practiced yet this week, Smith thanks to his lingering hamstring injury and Wicks with an ankle.

That leaves Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, and Brown as healthy and available wide receivers.

Is this the week Brown gets his chance?

 “I hope so,” he said. “If it does, I’ll try to make the most of it. And if it doesn’t, I’ll be rooting on my teammates.”

If Brown doesn’t figure into the Eagles’ plans there is a trade deadline coming up in a few weeks, and it’s possible to see a scenario where Howie Roseman unloads someone like Brown for a late-round draft pick.

Brown isn’t looking for a change of scenery, but he does want to play.

“I’m here right now just trying to play,” he said. “Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play, but at the ultimate end of the day, it’s not my plan. So I might want to play, I might want to contribute, but if that’s not the plan for me, I can’t dwell on it too much or you’ll be unhappy

“And then you’re taking that back home. I can’t take that back home to the wife and kids. So I gotta try to stay as positive as I can.”

How are you doing with that?

“Some days better than others,” he said with a laugh.

“But like I said, it’s a good group here with my teammates. If I’m frustrated, I can go talk to the coach. Everybody hears me out, so it’s not really a bad thing. We’re all dealing with something and we’re dealing with something as a team. So I don’t wanna add that extra stress.”

item.title: UConn tops UMass, 35-16
item.description: The Huskies were in complete control after scoring two TDs late in the second quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The UConn Huskies (4-3) defeated the UMass Minutemen (4-4), 35-16, to win their fourth straight over the Minutemen.

Quarterback Kalieb Osborne completed 14 of 19 (73.7%) passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns. Cyncir Bowers led the way on the ground with 132 rushing yards, while Osborne added 81 yards and both scored a touchdown. JD Willoughby tallied 65 yards and a touchdown to lead the Husky receivers.

Defensively, the Huskies held UMass to just 53 rushing yards. The visitors came into the game averaging 160.1 rushing yards per contest. The defense notched a pair of sacks but no turnovers, holding the Minutemen scoreless for nine straight possessions after allowing a field goal on the opening drive.

“We really challenged them to throw the ball,” head coach Jason Candle said. “When you’re able to compress the pocket and do a good job not allowing an athletic quarterback to escape to his dominant hand, it really takes an unselfish approach by the defensive front.”

UMass QB William “Pop” Watson III started his first game after missing the last two, completing 22 of 38 (57.9%) passes for 205 yards and a touchdown that came when the score was 28-3 in the third quarter.

On that first drive, Watson nailed wide-open wideout Drew Alsup down the middle for 23 yards. A trick-play pass to Watson got them to the 18-yard line before a pass to tight end Max Dowling at the 5-yard line. UConn’s defense held at the goal-line to keep them out of the end zone.

Connecticut began its first drive with a false start. However, Ky Wilson drew a pass interference that got them to midfield. Then, Shamar Porter caught an 11-yard pass and Bowers hurdled over a defender to get to the 38-yard marker. Osborne connected with Porter again for a 5-yard touchdown to get it to 7-3 at the end of the first quarter.

In the second quarter, seven consecutive three-and-outs occurred across both teams. Until the two-minute warning, the Huskies entered enemy territory once. They got good field position after a punt, on their own 45. After some Bowers runs got them to the 20-yard line, Osborne threw an over-the-shoulder pass to Willoughby for a touchdown, making it 14-3.

With a minute and a half before halftime, the defense forced another three-and-out, getting the ball back with a little over a minute left.

On the first play, Bowers rushed up the middle, danced around some defenders, and then bolted for a 70-yard house call. At 7-3 before the two-minute timeout, the score was 21-3 at halftime after Bowers’ second 70-plus-yard TD of the year.

On UMass’ second offensive possession in the third quarter, Porter blocked Edward Phillipson’s punt and recovered it in the endzone. Midway through the third quarter, UConn led 28-3. The Huskies’ last blocked punt for a touchdown was in 2012 against UMass.

“I always saw a willing blocker and a guy that was able to make contested catches,” Candle said of Porter. “With Javon [Brown] out, he’s had to step up and has continued doing a really good job being the main X receiver.”

With five and a half minutes remaining in the third period, from the 24-yard line, Jack O’Connor missed the field goal. The Minutemen took over and receiver Joseph Griffin Jr. reeled in a 41-yard pass down the sideline. Watson finished the drive with a touchdown pass to Curtis Kimmons IV to make it 28-9 after a missed conversion.

Osborne’s rushing TD capped off a drive where the Huskies were getting yards in chunks, making it 35-9 before another garbage time TD from the minutemen got us to the final score.

Next up, the Huskies travel to face the Air Force Falcons on Saturday, Oct. 31 at 3 p.m. The game will be televised on Mountain West Plus.

item.title: Seahawks sent mixed signals about whether Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday
item.description: The Seahawks sent plenty of mixed signals this week regarding the question of whether running back Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks sent plenty of mixed signals this week regarding the question of whether running back Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday. On Friday, the decision came.

He will not play.

Charbonnet, who suffered a torn ACL in the divisional-round win over the 49ers in January, returned to practice on October 1. He was moved to the active roster this week, and he fully participated in practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.

“Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that is exciting.”

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Macdonald's explanation created the impression that Charbonnet not playing on Sunday was the plan all along.

"We’re going along with the plan," Macdonald said. "Plan was to get a great week’s worth of work and see where we’re at. We’re going to take it into next week. It’s part of the plan. Zach’s doing great and we’ll go into next week and see how it goes.”

The situation doesn't violate the injury-reporting rules, even if the Seahawks arguably created the impression Charbonnet would play.

Actually, the Seahawks could have milked the uncertainty for two more days. Charbonnet could have been listed as questionable on Friday, with the decision announced on Sunday that he won't be among the active players.

Still, it feels odd. Especially since Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL said on Friday's Pat McAfee Show that Rapoport expects Charbonnet to "play and play a lot" on Sunday night. (The clip apparently was deleted from Twitter, but it's still in the YouTube version of the episode.)

At a time when more and more fans are skeptical of the impact of gambling and prediction-market influences on the flow of information (and/or misinformation), this is another tangible piece of grist for the tinfoil-hat mill.

item.title: President Trump on Sunday's game in Paris: "The NFL probably could have postponed"
item.description: The NFL plans to press forward with Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL plans to press forward with Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris.

Asked about the situation by reporters on Friday, President Trump expressed misgivings about the decision.

“Well, you worry about it," he said. "It's not — I think maybe it’s looking like tomorrow's gonna be a bad day in France. So you worry about it. I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, if you want to know the truth. Because France is really in trouble."

Postponement isn't really possible, given the NFL's schedule. Relocation would make the most sense, with the game moving to one of the two NFL-ready stadiums in London. (As best we can tell, both Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Wembley Stadium are available.)

For now, the NFL's attitude is "the show must go on." Even if the show could end up being something far different than what the NFL has envisioned.

item.title: 49ers injury report for Week 7 vs. Falcons: Nick Bosa, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel all out
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers have ruled out several stars for the Week 7 game against the Atlanta Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers face one of their toughest challenges of the 2026 season in their Week 7 matchup on the road against the Atlanta Falcons.

San Francisco is going into the game shorthanded with fewer than 48 players available, their undefeated record (6-0) on the line.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan has ruled out a handful of stars, including their main receivers. A few others are questionable for Sunday. He's discussed the need for players to stay ready because it's likely their number is called Sunday.

"It's stuff we've talked about throughout the week. Hope it doesn't get to it, and odds are it won't, but it definitely could," Shanahan said when asked if guys are ready to assume roles they don't usually play. "You're always a few injuries away from those situations and now it comes down to a couple. So, percentages go up."

Wide receivers Deebo Samuel Sr. and Mike Evans have been ruled out, Shanahan said after Friday's practice.

Additional players that will sit out include star defensive lineman Nick Bosa, linebacker Garret Wallow, safety Marques Sigle and linebacker Luke Gifford.

Cornerbacks Siran Neal and Upton Stout are questionable for the game, as is wide receiver Christian Kirk.

Shanahan says the message is to not have a letdown game. The Falcons are 2-4, but Shanahan doesn't want the 49ers to overlook them.

"That's something we talk about a lot. It's every week. I think that's the hardest thing about the NFL, just how much a game takes out of people, how much a week of preparation takes out of people and how much doing it 17 times does," Shanahan told reporters. "That's what I think is one of our strengths. I think we’ve got guys who understand how this league works. They understand what has to go into it and they know that anyone can beat you."

"I think when you have situations where we've won a number of games and we've got a bye-week ahead of us, it really helps when you can turn on the film and just show them," he added. "When you turn on Atlanta's film, they know how big of a challenge this is. We've got a number of guys down. We know they do, too, but they're a team that, I know the record doesn't show it, but they're a team that should be there in the end."

item.title: John Harbaugh makes Tom Brady reference for J.J. McCarthy — but it’s not what you think
item.description: Brady, 49, threw his final pass in 2022. And if he wanted to unretire?
item.content:encoded:
If John Harbaugh were picking between two Michigan-bred quarterbacks this week, the Giants would start J.J. McCarthy over Tom Brady. 

Access the Giants like never before

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

tRY IT NOW

Harbaugh, who made the change from Jameis Winston to McCarthy to start against the Texans, had some fun after Friday’s practice when using Brady as a random example of whether some roster moves can be made too soon or too early within the window of opportunity. 

“If Tom Brady decided he wanted to come back from retirement — which, I doubt for one second he could, no matter what he thinks,” Harbaugh said, turning to look directly into the camera. “You heard me, Tom.” 

Doubting Brady didn’t work out well for all the teams that let him fall to the No. 199 pick in the 2000 draft and then watched him win seven Super Bowls. Or for the teams that didn’t pursue him in 2020 free agency, when he jumped from the Patriots to the Buccaneers. 

Brady, 49, threw his final pass in 2022. And if he wanted to unretire? 

“I don’t think he’d be ready the first week, as much as you might want to put him in there,” Harbaugh said. “So, it wouldn’t be in the best interest to play the first week.” 

Brady was 6-5 in his illustrious career against Harbaugh’s Ravens. 

CB Paulson Adebo (knee) is expected to be activated off injured reserve after missing the past five games. His return Sunday will coincide with the loss of CB Greg Newsome II (concussion). 

Adebo, who is in the second year of a three-year, $54 million contract, lost his starting job to Deonte Banks in training camp and allowed two catches on three targets off the bench when called upon Week 1. 

“He’s ready to go,” Harbaugh said. “He’s a legit corner. He’s a cover corner, he tackles. He’s been a high-end corner in this league. I think he’s really determined to play that way. I think he’s finally probably healthy and ready to go. I can’t wait to see it. It looks like it’s going to be Sunday.” 

Harbaugh explained for the first time his reasoning behind this week’s release of RB Najee Harris, who was the starter last week. He said it was not because Harris criticized the four-man rotation after the game. 

“It was more about just, ‘All right, we’re going to set a course, and it’s hard to carry four backs,’ ” Harbaugh said. “There were some other moves we had to make to get guys on the roster. 

“Like I told him, nothing against what he did. I thought he ran super hard. I didn’t think he had a lot of [running] room, in all fairness, in the plays he happened to have in the last couple of weeks, but it was just the direction we decided to go at this time going forward. So, nothing that he did or didn’t do.” 

In addition to LB Tremaine Edmunds, who suffered a season-ending shoulder injury, and Newsome, the Giants could be without TE Theo Johnson (neck). He is doubtful. 

Adebo (knee) is officially listed as questionable, along with RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), S Jevón Holland (concussion), S Tyler Nubin (neck) and OT Marcus Mbow (knee).

item.title: Adonai Mitchell’s long-awaited Jets return from mystery finger injury gives offense the boost it needs
item.description: Adonai Mitchell may have been dealing with more than a finger injury. It appears he also has a case of amnesia — at least when it comes to the finger on his right hand that has kept him out of action for four games.
item.content:encoded:
Adonai Mitchell may have been dealing with more than a finger injury. It appears he also has a case of amnesia — at least when it comes to the finger on his right hand that has kept him out of action for four games. 

The Jets’ No. 2 receiver addressed the media Friday for the first time since sustaining the mystery injury in late September. But Mitchell didn’t recall how he hurt the finger, if an operation was a must as he remained sidelined or any other details regarding the injury. 

Take flight with the Jets

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

tRY IT NOW

“I really can’t even think back that far,” Mitchell said. “I’ve been so focused on what I want to do, which is to be back out there with the guys. That really slipped my mind.” 

Asked if he was surprised that he missed so much time, he said: “To be honest with you, I really can’t tell you. I’ve just been so locked in and so ready to get back and help the team. That’s all I’ve been thinking about. That’s all I can think about.” 

Most importantly to the Jets, Mitchell is ready to return Sunday against the Dolphins at MetLife Stadium. He practiced fully Friday. 

Asked how the finger feels when catching passes, the speedy receiver said: “I feel great, man. I got 10 of them things. I’m just ready to ball with the guys.” 

Head coach Aaron Glenn initially listed Mitchell as day to day after he popped up on the injury list Sept. 24. Glenn said Mitchell got his finger caught in a teammate’s jersey. He didn’t play that Sunday against the Lions. A few weeks later, the team acknowledged Mitchell underwent a minor procedure. 

Getting Mitchell back will give the Jets their full allotment of pass catchers for the first time since the opening drive of Week 1. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. suffered an ankle injury in that game, and didn’t return until last Sunday’s loss to the Patriots, when the first-round pick hauled in six passes for 103 yards and a touchdown. 

The offense has struggled to put the ball in the end zone in recent weeks, managing only four touchdowns over the last three games. On the season, the Jets are averaging 18.7 points, the sixth-lowest mark in the league. Over the first two weeks with a healthy Mitchell, they put up a combined 40 points. Mitchell, the Jets’ top deep threat, caught nine passes for 123 yards in those contests. 

“I can’t even put into words how excited I am,” Mitchell said. “I think we have all the pieces that we need, and I just can’t wait.” 

Said Geno Smith: “With all the playmakers that we have, when you have a guy like AD out there, he can stretch the field, he can be a possession guy, and I think him, Garrett [Wilson], Coop, they just present a lot of different challenges for the defense. And so the more guys, the merrier.” 

The 2-4 Jets find themselves at a crucial juncture of the season, with two home games against beatable opponents, the Browns and Raiders. It is a chance for them to get back to .500. Mitchell is eager to make an impact. 

“I’m feeling great,” he said. “I just want to help the team, contribute to some W’s. That’s all I’ve been thinking about.”

item.title: Three teams could be undefeated through seven weeks, which is a rarity
item.description: Entering Week 7, three teams are undefeated.
item.content:encoded:
Entering Week 7, three teams are undefeated. If three teams exit Week 7 undefeated, it will be a rarity.

The 49ers take their 6-0 record to Atlanta. The 5-0 Chiefs face the Seahawks in Seattle. The 5-0 Vikings play the Colts in Minneapolis.

Via NBC Sports research, only twice since the merger have three or more teams been undefeated through seven weeks of a season (with the exception of the 1982 strike year).

In 2009, three teams were unbeaten through seven weeks: the Saints, Colts, and Broncos. In 2015, five teams were perfect through seven weeks: the Panthers, Packers, Broncos, Patriots, and Bengals.

On both occasions, two of the unbeaten teams through seven weeks made it to the Super Bowl. In 2009, it was the Colts and the Saints. In 2015, the Panthers and the Broncos played in the Super Bowl.

The 49ers last went 7-0 in 2019. That year, they made it to the Super Bowl, losing to the Chiefs. The Chiefs last went 6-0 in 2024, when they made it to the Super Bowl for the third straight year, losing to the Eagles. The Vikings last went 6-0 in 2009. They lost to the Saints in the NFC Championship.

item.title: NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries?
item.description: The Falcons enter the unenviable situation of needing a win against an undefeated 49ers team that has pretty consistently looked like one of the NFL’s best units.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Falcons are sitting at 2-4 after a disappointing two-week stretch. Atlanta desperately needed to find a win over the past few weeks, instead dropping a game to the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens and (understandably) to the finally healthy Bears. The Falcons didn’t play terribly in either game, but in both, it was too little too late from Atlanta’s offense.

TNow the team enters the unenviable situation of needing a win against an undefeated 49ers team that has pretty consistently looked like one of the NFL’s best units despite a growing injury list. That lengthy injury list, along with some rest and off-field advantages, could help the Falcons pull off the unlikely upset in Week 7. The bettors seem to think so as well, as Atlanta is just a 2.5-point home underdog according to FanDuel.

Falcons vs 49ers predictions

On paper, the 49ers are clearly the superior team. San Francisco is one of only a handful of teams who are top-10 in both offense and defense, and one of only two who are top-5 in both categories. To put it simply, there aren’t any obvious glaring weaknesses on this team—except their long injury list, which is only growing heading into Week 7. That’s something the Falcons will have to take advantage of to come away with an improbable victory.

The 49ers offense struggled mightily once Mike Evans, who Falcons fans know quite well, left the game against the Commanders in Week 6. Washington was close to mounting a comeback, but was ultimately unsuccessful due to their own issues. Evans, along with Deebo Samuel, have both been declared out for Week 7. Those are major losses, and when combined with San Francisco’s other injuries at the position, could be too much for the passing game to overcome.

Atlanta is dealing with their own injury problems, particularly on defense. Starting slot corner Billy Bowman and linebacker Divine Deablo are both out, and three other cornerbacks are questionable. It does sound like A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson are likely to play on Sunday, but a new injury (and questionable designation) for rookie Avieon Terrell throw a wrench into things. Veteran Mike Hughes, who has struggled mightily this season, will be on track to start again unless those players are cleared.

Already down Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr., Atlanta is looking at questionable designations for Za’Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam on the edge. Standout interior pass rusher Gervon Dexter Sr. also picked up a questionable tag heading into the weekend. Atlanta is perilously thin on the edge and can’t afford any more losses here.

If Atlanta can get most of these players in the game on Sunday, they may have a significant health advantage over San Francisco. History is also unkind to West Coast teams traveling to play in the 1pm timeslot on the East Coast, and the 49ers are working off a rest disadvantage after just playing on Monday Night Football. Health and extra rest could be critical to the Falcons pulling off the upset.

That’ll, plus Atlanta figuring out how to deal with blitz pressure and opposing defenses crowding the line of scrimmage. Michael Penix Jr. has been outstanding when kept clean this season, but he’s absolutely cratered when faced with pressure. Part of the issue is that Atlanta has been allowing the fastest time to pressure in the NFL by quite a wide margin, giving Penix little time to react. Hopefully that’s been a major point of emphasis in practice this week.

I’m not confident in Atlanta’s ability to take down a superior opponent, especially coming off the past two weeks. So I’m going to say that the 49ers should win this game. However, Atlanta’s potential health advantage along with the extra rest and the West Coast-East Coast factors could combine to give the Falcons a real shot in this one. Plus, Evan would be remiss if I didn’t mention the RED HELMET ENERGY. It’s uncanny, but the Falcons typically play great in this uniform. Will they pull it off? That’s the question I don’t feel confident answering.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders unionize, will collectively bargain with team

The most famous cheerleading crew in the country is celebrating a win – but it's not a Dallas Cowboys victory.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and the team jointly announced Friday, Oct. 23 the creation of a labor union representing the cheerleaders that will collectively bargain with the team, the most valuable professional sports franchise in the world. The Cowboys are recognizing the union and the new, independent group is called the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA).

— jen ramos-eisen (@jenramose) October 23, 2026

"The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit," the announcement read. "They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide."

The cheerleaders have recently been featured on a Netflix docuseries "America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders" (and have appeared on many other programs over the years). Season 2 chronicled the dancers' quest for improved salaries, with The Dallas Morning News reporting that the cheerleaders said they were due a 400% raise for the 2025 season. In 2024, The New York Times reported that a fifth-year cheerleader made $15 per hour and $500 for each appearance.

The Cowboys had no further comment when contacted by USA TODAY Sports.

This is not the NFL's first cheerleading union, however. In 1995, the Buffalo Bills' group – the "Jills," which disbanded in 2014 amid claims of mistreatment and underpay – won a ruling with the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) to become the first union representing cheerleading squads.

item.title: Bills’ Sam Franklin gets spitting suspension overturned after winning appeal
item.description: The Bills’ spitting scandal has come to a close.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills’ spitting scandal has come to a close.

Bills defensive back Sam Franklin got his one-game suspension overturned Friday, winning an appeal to the NFL after the league penalized him for allegedly spitting at an opposing player during Buffalo’s Week 6 win over the Raiders.

Rather than a suspension, the NFL reduced Franklin’s punishment to a $14,926 fine, according to a statement from the league.

The league announced Wednesday that they were suspending Franklin, 30, for one game for seemingly spitting on Las Vegas offensive lineman DJ Glaze after an extra point attempt in the fourth quarter of the Bills’ 33-30 victory.

Video of the play shows the two getting into it following the kick, but it’s unclear whether Franklin actually spat on Glaze.

Upon the suspension being overturned, Franklin’s agents again vehemently denied the spitting allegations, adding that they are “glad” that the ordeal is over.

“As we said from the start, Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did,” Franklin’s agents Harold C. Lewis and Christian Addison said in a statement to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. “We’re glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review.

“It’s unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely.”

They also brought attention to Glaze’s actions towards Franklin during the play.

“We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player’s conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game,” the statement added. “We’re glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday.”

The NFL also suspended Franklin’s teammate C.J. Gardner-Johnson for a game after he was ejected for spitting in the same game.

Gardner-Johnson appeared to spit at Raiders tight end Brock Bowers in the third quarter, prompting his ejection.

Unlike Franklin, however, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension was upheld on Thursday.

item.title: Bears vs. Patriots Game Balls: A Signature Victory
item.description: After an exciting win over the Patriots, @ryandroste hands out his Chicago #Bears Week 7 game balls.
item.content:encoded:
This week’s Thursday Night Football victory for the Chicago Bears over the New England Patriots will go down as one of the team’s signature victories of 2026.

The reigning AFC champions came into Soldier Field on a short week and with a long list of injuries. The Bears, though, were also no strangers to the injury report, missing key contributors such as RB Kyle Monangai, DE Dayo Odeyingbo, as well as LB Jack Sanborn and original starting LT Braxton Jones, among others (S Coby Bryant has yet to play this season). Plus, DE Montez Sweat was out for the final game of his two-game suspension.

And then there’s QB Caleb Williams, who returned on Sunday from a hamstring injury that he can still be seen favoring at times if you look close enough. But that didn’t stop the team from winning the game from bell to bell, and although things tightened up at the end, the Bears showed once again that they know how to play with a lead. That’s a diversion from last year, when the team’s calling card was coming from behind to win games.

Let’s get to this week’s game balls.

Offense Game Ball: WR Luther Burden III

This award could go to Caleb Williams pretty much every week, and this week was no exception. Williams was terrific once again, but we’re going to look to WR Luther Burden III who had his best game of the young season.

Burden was the team’s key target in the first half, and he scored the Bears’ second touchdown of the game when he received a short pass from Williams that he broke into a 24 yard touchdown reception. That touchdown made the score 20-7 with 14 seconds left in the first half.

In addition to his touchdown in the second quarter, Burden also had a 58 yard reception late in the first quarter that was nearly a touchdown.

Burden ended the night with four catches for 130 yards, one touchdown, and one run for seven yards.

Defense Game Ball: LB D’Marco Jackson

Jackson continues to be a heck of a find for the Bears, who claimed the former New Orleans Saint last year off of waivers and saw him work his way up the depth chart due to injuries, elevating his game in the process. He’s become one of the team’s most dependable players on defense.

Jackson picked off QB Drake Maye in the end zone, stopping a potential Patriots scoring drive that could have ended up swinging the game. With a touchdown and successful extra point on that drive, the Patriots would have gone up 14-13. It was Maye’s first interception in three weeks.

Jackson is signed with the Bears through the 2027 season, having signed a two year extension back in March, but the team might want to start thinking about keeping him around even longer.

Special Teams Game Ball: K Cairo Santos

I went back and forth on this one a little bit. Santos made a clutch 58 yard field goal (his career long) to ice the game toward the end of the fourth quarter, but the reason the team badly needed those points was because Santos had missed a 53 yarder just a few minutes earlier in the fourth quarter.

In the end, I felt Santos was deserving due to the fact that his prior miss would have caused a lesser player to shrink under the pressure.

But Santos wanted the pressure. In fact, he seemed to relish it. Santos told Bears special teams coach Richard Hightower he was ready to kick the field goal, and head coach Ben Johnson trusted his guy.

Right down the middle. Never a doubt.

Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.

item.title: Aaron Glenn faces $250K fine for conduct toward NFL officials
item.description: Aaron Glenn was one of three head coaches fined $250,000 by the league for conduct toward game officials, a source confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Glenn was one of three head coaches fined $250,000 by the league for conduct toward game officials, a source confirmed. 

Take flight with the Jets

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

tRY IT NOW

The Jets were whistled for five penalties for 35 yards in the loss to the Patriots, including a questionable offensive pass interference on receiver Tim Patrick that wiped out an Omar Cooper Jr. touchdown on the first drive of the game. 

Glenn does not have to immediately pay the fine. It is on hold for the time being and can be repealed with good behavior. The NFL is trying to make a point to coaches regarding their treatment of officials. Glenn declined to comment directly about the fine but did address his relationship with officials. 

“I don’t think that’s ever been a problem at all. Listen, I understand how the league works and I am fully behind how the league operates and I don’t think any coach within this league has any issues with the refs,” Glenn said on Friday. “We know it’s a tough game and refs make those split-second calls at that time. It’s tough. So we support the refs, we support what the league’s doing. 

“And, again, I keep those things between me, the refs and the NFL.” 

No. 1 running back Breece Hall (quad) was limited in practice for the second consecutive day. He is questionable to play Sunday after missing the last three games. 

“We’ll take it all the way to Sunday and see how he feels,” Glenn said. 

The same applies to starting left guard Dylan Parham (knee). Running back/kick returner Kene Nwangwu (knee) is also questionable. Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion) and edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) all were ruled out. 

Glenn said that Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was not benched at the end of the loss to the Patriots. There are different defensive packages in which Brownlee and rookie cornerback D’Angelo Ponds are on the field. They are the team’s two defensive backs who are used on the inside against slot receivers. 

“Both of those guys will play,” Glenn said.

item.title: NFL predictions: With the defense cooking, will the Browns-Titans matchup be put to bed early?
item.description: Can the Browns finally win a game by double digits?
item.content:encoded:
This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (4-2) take on the Tennessee Titans (1-5). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game.

Browns’ Defense is Cooking…

…except for the start of football games. In four of their six games, including their last three games, this has been the result of the opposing team’s opening drive:

Week 1, Jaguars: 8 plays, 59 yards (Touchdown)
Week 4, Steelers: 17 plays, 73 yards (Touchdown)
Week 5, Jets: 8 plays, 90 yards (Touchdown)
Week 6, Ravens: 11 plays, 66 yards (Touchdown)

In that first game, the defense was just bad the whole first half. In the other three games, they did a pretty solid-to-dominant job the rest of the way. I’ve harped a bunch of times this season on how much I value the adjustments that Mike Rutenburg has this defense making in-game, which is something I thought I never saw from Jim Schwartz. We’re also seeing where a defensive front is not reliant on one guy (Myles Garrett) to save the day. Players are collectively stepping up and rallying together, and you’re also seeing great individual efforts out of the likes of Denzel Ward, Carson Schewesinger, and Maliek Collins. This week, the Browns get Mason Graham back, who looked like a beast to begin his second year before hurting his knee.

With the defense playing so well, it’s also encouraging this week that they are facing the 32nd-ranked offense in the NFL. Cam Ward hasn’t been able to muster much in the passing game. Also last year, RB Tony Pollard had his best game of the season against Cleveland, going off for 161 yards on 25 carries with 2 touchdowns. Hopefully, that element can be contained, especially with help returning at defensive tackle.

But the Offense Needs to do More

The fourth quarter, game-winning drives have happened four times this season, which is great on one hand. It almost happened a fifth time (the loss to the Jets). On the other hand, we’re starting to reach a bit of a tipping point on needing to see more productivity and points on the board in the rest of the game. Over those first few games of the season, the feeling was, ‘Alright, we’re seeing some encouraging things, maybe as the offense continues to build a rhythm, we’ll see better results.’ Instead, things have gotten pretty stagnant from an overall game perspective.

  • Cleveland has scored 12 and 13 points in their last two games, fortunate to have gone 1-1 during that stretch. Over the last three weeks, Cleveland is the only team to have a victory on the board after scoring that few of points. The last team that won with that low of a point total was the Giants back in Week 3, when they won 12-7 over…the Titans. In other words, Cleveland was lucky to scoot by with a victory in that sense last week, and if their offense is not better, even against the Titans, you’re going to have teams beating you.
  • What can get better? Last week, one of the adjustments seems to have been getting Jerry Jeudy more involved in the game again. The running game also showed some progress, but ironically enough, many fans feel that was becauseQuinshon Judkins was out, and Jaleel McLaughlin was back. I’m not trying to be a Judkins hater by any means — like I’ve said multiple times, I thought he looked very sharp last year, and this year, I think he looks as pedestrian as you can get. Dylan Sampson might also return this week.
  • Something is off that KC Concepcion is six games in, and has 186 yards receiving (average of 31 yards receiving per game). I go back to what I saw from him in training camp, and I know that was just training camp, but my takeaway multiple times was, ‘This guy is something special.’ And it’s also not like I say that about every receiver that comes through the team because I’m a homer. I don’t think I’ve ever felt that about a receiver in camp. And during the regular season, I think he’s looked the part still — it’s just, tying in with the rest of the offense, the production isn’t there yet.
  • Harold Fannin, also, has 2 catches for 13 yards in the last two games. The Titans have defended tight ends fairly well this year, so I don’t know if there’s a breakout to be expected this week, but the young tight end needs to get involved more.
  • Tennessee picked up their first win of the season last week, but their offense didn’t find themselves. They were shut out 13-0 at the half, then forced a fumble, got an interception (which both led to field goals), and then blocked a punt for a touchdown, to generate points. That should be a talking point for the Browns this week, but if they protect the ball and are diligent about special teams assignments like they’ve been, Tennessee’s offense shouldn’t beat them.
  • According to FanDuel, the Browns are 1.5 point favorites against the Titans. The over/under is 37.5.

Quick Hitters

Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about getting his top two running backs returning this week:

Yeah, it’s huge. I mean, it’s obviously our top two backs. So, yeah, those two are a big part of what we do on offense, run and pass. And they’re also, we talked about this last week too, a little bit of a one-two punch, if you will, whatever you want to call it. They have different skill sets that we can utilize for both of them. So, yeah, having those guys back is going to be huge.

Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg talked about Emmanuel McNeil-Warren getting a lot of action last week after Grant Delpit exited early:

I mean, he did a great job in the game. Was excellent with his communication, was excellent with his assignments, and then you saw his playmaking ability come to life. But that goes back to him continuing to build his confidence. You saw it earlier in the year on special teams, playing really, really well on special teams, getting more opportunities on defense, playing really well in practice, and him transferring that to the game. And he’s going to continue going this way because of, number one, just who he is. He wants to be coached, he wants the information, he wants to be challenged, he wants to be told when it’s good, when it’s bad. And then you can see his play continuing to rise because of who he is.

Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer was asked about Corey Bojorquez not having his best game last week:

“Yeah, I mean, we didn’t think it was, he could have…He had more opportunities that he could have taken advantage of. It’s the minus, the two minus-45 kicks, where you’re like, we’ve got to have those balls inside the 20-yard line. And that’s what I told him after the game, looking at it, it’s like, ‘we’ve got to get the ball inside the 20 on those’, because if you get the ball inside the 20 on those, you’ve got four inside the 20 for the game. And you only gave up, I think it was like 7.5 yards per return, and so if you handled those punts better, you’re looking at the game completely differently. But we talked about it, and really just trying to keep the ball from going out of bounds so early, because you leave it up to the official to mark wherever he thinks it goes out. Now, I think there is some technology to it now that we learned, but he’s got to do a better job of keeping it in play. And we’ve proven now with Malachi (Corley) that we can down the punt inside the 10-yard line. So, I think we learned from that and we’ll see improvement from us.”

Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN:

Predictions

Chris Pokorny: “Many are predicting this to be a close game, with Cleveland squeaking out a win. I can’t blame them, considering the Browns’ four victories have been by a combined 13 points. But with the momentum the Browns continue to build, I feel like their defense is rocking with confidence this week, and the offense finds a slight groove to make this a double digit win.” Browns 27, Titans 10

Jared Mueller: “A road game with a bit of weird attached to it with the Jordan Elliott release from the Titans and his history with the Browns.

This seems similar to the game versus the Jets; the Browns seem to stay close to their opponent for a variety of reasons, and can struggle to put things away. Tennessee is coming off their first victory and a young team can get on a roll quickly. If Quincy Williams’ neck injury leads to him missing the game, Cleveland’s defense all of a sudden has a big, important question mark. 

As of now, the weather looks like it will be perfect in Nashville, with a high of 77 degrees. That will help the Browns offense get going a bit.” Browns 24, Titans 20

Curtiss Brown: “The last time these two teams played, Cleveland couldn’t stop the run for whatever reason. The Titans aren’t an abject disaster but its hard to say this team has looked better than last year. A case can be made they look worse. However, the team was able to get a win against the Indianapolis Colts so they aren’t completely bad. 

As for the Browns, its hard to say that they are a good football team. They aren’t bad but they aren’t necessarily good. Mediocre at best is fine. The Titans will give this team fits (mainly on defense) but the Browns defense has to be prepared for quarterback Cam Ward. If the offense can find some consistency and play a complete game that would be nice. Could be a close game but Cleveland barely wins. I could be wrong though.” Browns 23, Titans 20

Barry Shuck: “After the schedule came out, I looked at the Browns opponents. They are playing that last place schedule, which means, except for the Cardinals and Dolphins, they play every division cellar dweller from last year. I looked at what Todd Monken had done with virtually every offensive unit he has been charged of. Every single team’s offense improved tremendously. So, I predicted Cleveland could take the bad teams, split within the division, then come out with a 12-5-0 record. However, one of those wins was supposed to the Jets. And after a 2-4-0 start, the Jets remain a bad team. This brings up the Titans, who just might be the worst team in the league. Which, the Browns should win, right? My memory still is on how Cleveland gave up their soul against New York, and floundered. A 38-14 win for the Browns? Or a 17-13 heartbreaker to a horrible club instead? Which offense shows up?” Browns 24, Titans 24

Who do you think will win, Browns fans? Let us know in the comments section below.

item.title: CeeDee Lamb has ‘why not us’ attitude for Cowboys’ NFC East chances despite worrying skid
item.description: He isn't phased by the Cowboys’ two-game losing streak.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb isn’t phased by his team’s two-game losing streak.

When speaking to reporters on Friday ahead of Dallas’ Week 7 matchup against the Eagles, Lamb insisted that the NFC East is still up for grabs despite the Cowboys’ 2-4 record on the year.

“Anybody can win this division, so why not us?” Lamb said, according to ESPN.

Lamb added that he believes the Cowboys have time to turn things around because other teams in the division have been playing poorly, with the Giants leading the pack at a modest 3-2-1 thus far.

“Very fortunate that everybody else is playing pretty bad. But overall, just everything is still in front of us,” he added. “We still have our opportunity to do what we want to do, and that’s to get in the tournament, and it starts on Monday.

“So just shaking that back and getting back into the win column I feel like is the most important thing, and that’s been the point of emphasis this week.”

Despite going into this season with high expectations, the Cowboys’ defensive metrics are among the worst in the NFL, ranking 25th in points allowed per game (26.5), 30th in yards (382.5) and dead last in run defense (149.8 yards).

With their offense now stalling as well — scoring just 29 points combined in the last two games — the Cowboys’ next few weeks are crucial for remaining a division contender.

Quarterback Dak Prescott admitted that the mindset of the team is “determined, and I would hope urgent,” going into Monday’s game in Philadelphia.

“We can only say we’ve got a lot of games in front of us for so long. Might be already past us, right? We’ve got to go win,” Prescott said. “You’ve got to go win. You want to give yourself a chance to be a winning team, to be a playoff team.

“You got to win as many games as you can, and when you drop two games — in particular games that we didn’t expect to drop — it makes it that much harder. So urgent, urgent to get it done now.”

item.title: Raiders’ Dont’e Thornton running out of time as roster deadline looms
item.description: Time is running out on Dont’e Thornton. And with each passing week, it becomes harder to point to his health as the reason the Raiders wide receiver remains on injured...
item.content:encoded:
Time is running out on Dont’e Thornton.

And with each passing week, it becomes harder to point to his health as the reason the Raiders wide receiver remains on injured reserve.

By Thornton’s assessment, he is healthy. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak has said the same.

“Yeah, he’s healthy,” Kubiak said Friday.

There is also an obvious need at his position, where the Raiders are short on available bodies and need someone beyond Tre Tucker to emerge as a dependable contributor.

Healthy player. Clear need. Significant opportunity.

Yet Thornton remains on the outside looking in.

“He will not be activated for this game,” Kubiak said Friday.

That means Thornton will not be on the field in Sunday’s game against the Rams, extending his season-long absence and leaving him little time to convince the Raiders he belongs on the field.

“He’s making big progress,” Kubiak said. “He’s done a lot of good things in practice. Still working back into getting his football legs back after missing a lot of time. But I’ve been really pleased with his effort, with his detail. He’s close.”

Just not close enough to be activated yet, which seems significant given the Raiders obvious needs in the wide receiver room, and the door they opened for Thornton to show he can contribute.

Now, a deadline is looming, and there is a very real possibility that Thornton’s season will end before it ever actually started.

The Raiders opened Thornton’s practice window Oct. 7, beginning the 21-day period in which they could evaluate him before deciding whether to activate him. That window closes Oct. 28.

If Thornton is not activated by then, he will remain on injured reserve for the rest of the season.

For a player drafted on potential, the possibility of losing an entire year of development is particularly troubling.

The Raiders selected Thornton in the fourth round of the 2025 draft out of Tennessee. The attraction was obvious.

At 6-foot-5, with a 4.30-second 40-yard dash, Thornton possessed an uncommon combination of height and speed.

But he arrived as more of a raw prospect than a finished receiver. The physical gifts were there. Turning them into consistent NFL production would require development.

Thornton finished his rookie season with 10 catches for 135 yards and no touchdowns in 15 games.

Those numbers underscored how much work remained. And while injuries have interrupted his second season, the breakthrough the Raiders envisioned has yet to materialize.

His current situation only sharpens that concern.

Kubiak has consistently said Thornton needs to show he is ready to play. Being healthy enough to practice does not automatically mean being ready to contribute on Sundays.

The Raiders have now had more than two weeks to evaluate him. Their decision to keep him off the roster for another game suggests he has yet to demonstrate what the coaching staff needs to see.

That does not establish precisely where Thornton is falling short. But with his health no longer the stated obstacle, the question becomes whether the Raiders trust him to help.

And another receiver could soon enter the picture.

Jack Bech, who suffered a broken forearm against the Saints, is eligible to return from injured reserve next week after missing the mandatory four games. Bech said he is good to go and eager to return.

His importance both in the pass game and as a run blocker, coupled with his special teams versatility, not only give Bech an advantage over Thornton in terms of a roster spot, they are big-time needs for the Raiders.

At this point, it would be a surprise if Bech wasn’t immediately added to the 53-man roster, which further clouds Thornton’s situation just as he reaches the end of his evaluation period.

The door remains open. Thornton still has an opportunity to turn his physical promise into something the Raiders can use.

But potential can only carry the conversation so far.

The Raiders need production. Thornton needs to show he can provide it.

And the clock is ticking.
